# Bloxwap HIG 0.1.0 candidate

## ADR 001: platform renderers, shared contracts
Source: docs/architecture/001-packages.md

# ADR 001: platform renderers, shared contracts

Status: accepted for candidate 0.1.0. Issues #4, #5. Evidence: `evidence/upstream-inventory.json`.

```mermaid
graph TD
  Tokens[HIG tokens] --> Web[HIG React]
  Tokens --> Native[HIG Native]
  Contracts[HIG contracts] --> Web
  Contracts --> Native
  Contracts --> Feedback[optional feedback adapters]
  Web --> Docs[docs and consumer fixtures]
  Native --> Expo[Expo gallery]
```

`@bloxwap/hig-tokens` owns palette, density, units and generation; `@bloxwap/hig-contracts` owns platform-neutral types and formatting. `@bloxwap/hig-react` and `@bloxwap/hig-native` own renderers. `@bloxwap/hig-feedback` owns optional adapter entry points. Base controls never load audio, haptics, charts, Expo or another platform. Each component has an individual export; CSS is explicit and side-effectful. Plain HTML consumers use tokens/CSS alone.

Candidate validation matrix: Node 22.22+, TypeScript 5.9, React/DOM 19.1, RN 0.81.5, Expo 54, Vite 6.4. Next 16.4.0 webpack is verified by M5 production/packed consumer checks. NativeWind styling remains outside the supported StyleSheet consumer path. Use StyleSheet on RN and plain CSS on web; Tailwind may refer to `var(--hig-*)` without scanning HIG sources. The pinned monorepo source now documents web/native rem roots of 16; see source reconciliation. Never infer native sizes by replacing `rem` with `dp`.

Prefer built-in semantic controls; modal/disclosure behavior must retain keyboard, focus restoration and descriptions. Optional chart entry imports the chart SDK only on the client. Libraries retain upstream licenses; extracted tokens and mark have commit provenance, no vendor engine source is copied. Font binaries remain owned by @bloxwap/font (OFL-1.1).

Deprecation plan: inventory all live references, map variants to intent/density, run migration diff and consumer validation, switch a pilot behind a host flag, then delete unused copies. App comfortable targets and Pro compact rows are intentional. HIG cannot retire owning-repository copies within this hig-only change. API/token/behavior changes follow semver; breaking accessibility behavior counts as breaking. Support upgrades require web, SSR and Metro evidence with a documented rollback before changing the matrix.


## Attribution and provenance
Source: docs/architecture/attribution.md

# Attribution and provenance

HIG code: MIT. @radix-ui/react-dialog, dropdown-menu, popover, tooltip: MIT, consumed as dependencies without copied engine code. @bloxwap/chart/sfx/haptic: independent upstream packages; optional integration only. @bloxwap/font: OFL-1.1, binaries stay in its pinned package. Brand SVG/geometry derives from Font docs, exact upstream commit in `evidence/upstream-inventory.json`; do not imply arbitrary trademark relicensing. Utility CheckIcon is original simple geometry. Full icons catalogs are excluded.

## Generated favicon and social preview

`npm run generate` derives unchanged SVG favicons and a 1200×630 SVG social preview from the approved mark. Source SHA256 and derivative paths are in `planning/brand-artifacts.json`; lint rejects stale outputs. The derived preview declares its lineage and omits the source credential metadata; unchanged source/favicons retain it. Hosts whose social crawlers require raster images must render a PNG from this same SVG instead of redrawing the mark. This preview uses a generic font rather than embedding the full font asset.


## Candidate platform support · 0.1.0
Source: docs/architecture/platform-matrix.md

# Candidate platform support · 0.1.0

| Area | DOM | RN | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Actions, surfaces, text, fields | Semantic DOM elements | Pressable/View/Text/TextInput | behavior tests, Vite/SSR/Metro |
| Native text scaling and script tracking | Browser zoom; no cap | `Text`/`Heading`/`NumberReadout` `maxFontSizeMultiplier` (prop or HIGProvider default); Korean/Chinese runs at companion spacing via `script` and `letterSpacingByScript` | native Jest (#67); iOS Simulator AX5: capped readout 48pt vs 86pt prose; Android emulator 200% (non-linear scaling stays under the 2x cap) (`evidence/native-sim/issue-67-71/`) |
| Native colour roles | CSS severity/data attributes | `Switch` `tone`, `Alert` `severity`/`tone` take token roles only; raw colours fall back. The Android Switch thumb uses the `text` token instead of the app theme accent | native Jest (#67); iOS Simulator and Android emulator captures (`evidence/native-sim/issue-67-71/`) |
| Selection/range | Built-in input/select | OS Switch/community Slider, radio/check Pressables, Modal chooser; Android Slider adds `ACTION_SET_PROGRESS` through the autolinked `HIGAdjustableView` (plain View without native linking) | contract tests; Android emulator UiAutomation (#71): set-progress listed, 80 applied once, snapped/clamped, absent and rejected while disabled; iOS Simulator increment/decrement unchanged (`evidence/native-sim/issue-67-71/`) |
| Dialog/sheet/menu | Radix scoped primitives | Modal and explicit close/back; optional Gorhom GestureSheet entry | DOM nested focus/Escape; mocked native focus/back/detents plus separate packed Android/iOS gesture entry |
| Tooltip/popover | Radix hover/focus/anchored | persistent HelpText/modal | no RN hover claim |
| Navigation/search | href/callback adapters | host route/back callbacks | tab/search/disclosure contracts |
| Financial lists/table | semantic table/list | FlatList labeled rows | formatting and contract tests |
| Chart | optional lazy @bloxwap/chart canvas | numeric/list summary only | typed theme; physical gesture evidence pending |
| Brand mark | individual SVG renderer/asset | optional react-native-svg | pinned geometry; device comparison pending |
| Fonts | pinned Sans/Mono asset URLs | hash-pinned static faces, typed manifest, explicit weight registration and host script fallback | Expo-web loading/byte/hash gates; no physical native-font certification |

SSR: client components retain use-client boundaries in emitted JS. Importing a button needs React/tokens/contracts only at runtime. CSS is explicitly imported. Native API never imports DOM, Web Audio or chart. Native target size remains comfortable even when host density is compact; Pro density is a DOM exception, not a reason to shrink phone targets.

Optional peer packages: chart only for chart entry; community Slider for native selection entry; react-native-svg for native brand entry. Gorhom/Reanimated/Worklets/Gesture Handler are isolated behind the optional gesture-sheet entry; base imports do not load them. No root barrel loads every component. DOM overlays are one scoped family entry and carry Radix MIT attribution; Radix peers are optional caret ranges and overlay-free web recipes have their own entries. ESM is supported; CommonJS consumer support is not claimed.


## Actions & surfaces · HIG 0.1.0
Source: docs/components/actions-surfaces.md

# Actions & surfaces · HIG 0.1.0

Buttons, typography, and layout primitives for clear actions and related content.

Includes `Button`, `IconButton`, `Link`, `Text`, `Heading`, `Stack`, `Inline`, `Surface`, `Card`, and `Separator`.

Issue #13. Entry: `button / surface`. Import platform entries from `@bloxwap/hig-react/button` or `@bloxwap/hig-native/button` according to applicability below. Import `@bloxwap/hig-react/css` once on web; tokens CSS is a separate explicit import.

## API and anatomy

| Component | Key props and behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `Button`, `IconButton` | `children`, `intent`, `busy`, `busyLabel`, `disabled`, `fullWidth`, `suppressFeedback`, and forwarded ref. Web uses `onClick`; native uses `onPress`. The busy suffix (` · Working`) comes from HIGProvider `messages.busy` or `busyLabel`; `''` hides it while busy state stays exposed. |
| `Link` | Platform link behavior; host applications own routing. |
| `Text`, `Heading` | Platform text props. Native adds `maxFontSizeMultiplier` (font-scale cap for dense numeric readouts, also on `NumberReadout`; HIGProvider sets a default) and `script` (`latin`, `ko`, `zh`; detected from string children). Korean and Chinese runs use the companion face's own spacing (`scriptLetterSpacing`, 0em) instead of Latin tracking; HIGProvider `letterSpacingByScript` overrides it per script in em. |
| `Stack`, `Inline`, `Surface`, `Card` | Platform layout props. |

## When to use and examples

Use one primary review action. Do: busy protects host requests and displays the translated busy label (`Working` in English). Don’t: use destructive red for every sell button.

## States, interaction and accessibility

DOM semantic button/anchor, forwarded focus, target min-height tied to density (web: 44px comfortable, 36px compact); RN target always at least 48. Multiline labels wrap; RN custom children render in a View with text nodes styled individually.

State review: rest; keyboard focus/hover (DOM); accepted press and release/cancel; selected/checked where applicable; disabled; busy; inline error/recovery; empty/loading; long translations/large text; reduced motion; sound and haptics disabled. No host action occurs on mere focus. Disabled/busy targets suppress accepted activation. Core has no required feedback backend; the optional provider callback follows the action, honors cancellation and isolates errors.

## Platform mapping and limits

RN external Link uses Linking; routes belong to host. Native fontFamily only after registration. Decorative SVG hidden; IconButton label is mandatory.

## Validation and citation

See `tests/components.dom.test.tsx`, `tests/native/components.test.cjs`, consumer fixtures and milestone evidence. Physical hardware, assistive-technology and baseline product comparisons are unperformed unless linked explicitly. Cite HIG 0.1.0 with this chapter anchor and a commit permalink, not a mutable preview branch. Preserve business behavior behind a host rollback flag during adoption.


## Charts · HIG 0.1.0
Source: docs/components/chart.md

# Charts · HIG 0.1.0

Web price charts with text summaries and native readout alternatives.

Includes web-only `PriceChart` and `chartTheme`. Native uses readouts, lists, and text summaries.

Issue #20. Entry: `chart`. Import platform entries from `@bloxwap/hig-react/chart` for the DOM canvas integration only. Native consumers use `@bloxwap/hig-native/data` for summary/readout/list alternatives. Import `@bloxwap/hig-react/css` once on web; tokens CSS is a separate explicit import.

## API and anatomy

| Component | Key props and behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `PriceChart` | `data`, required `summary`, `height`, and chart SDK props. |
| `chartTheme` | Token-based colors in sRGB for canvas compatibility. |

## When to use and examples

Do: provide host-generated price/trend summary and lazy-load chart on demand. Don’t: play effects on ticks or present web canvas as RN.

## States, interaction and accessibility

@bloxwap/chart/react loads only on PriceChart render, in Suspense. Token theme covers surface/text/border/grid/crosshair/up/down/fonts; engine owns gestures and cleanup.

State review: rest; keyboard focus/hover (DOM); accepted press and release/cancel; selected/checked where applicable; disabled; busy; inline error/recovery; empty/loading; long translations/large text; reduced motion; sound and haptics disabled. No host action occurs on mere focus. Disabled/busy targets suppress accepted activation. Core has no required feedback backend; the optional provider callback follows the action, honors cancellation and isolates errors.

## Platform mapping and limits

RN canvas is unsupported in this candidate. Use NumberReadout/List plus host summaries. A native chart engine/WebView bridge needs a separate supported target and device lifecycle review, rather than an invented integration.

## Validation and citation

See `tests/components.dom.test.tsx`, `tests/native/components.test.cjs`, consumer fixtures and milestone evidence. Physical hardware, assistive-technology and baseline product comparisons are unperformed unless linked explicitly. Cite HIG 0.1.0 with this chapter anchor and a commit permalink, not a mutable preview branch. Preserve business behavior behind a host rollback flag during adoption.


## Fields & inputs · HIG 0.1.0
Source: docs/components/fields.md

# Fields & inputs · HIG 0.1.0

Labeled inputs for text, search, and amounts, with visible help and validation.

Includes `Field`, `Label`, `Input`, `TextArea`, `AmountInput`, and `SearchInput`.

Issue #14. Entry: `field`. Import platform entries from `@bloxwap/hig-react/field` or `@bloxwap/hig-native/field` according to applicability below. Import `@bloxwap/hig-react/css` once on web; tokens CSS is a separate explicit import.

## API and anatomy

| Component | Key props and behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `Field` | `label`, `id` (web), `description`, `error`, `required`, and `disabled`. |
| `Input`, `TextArea` | Platform input props and forwarded refs. |
| `AmountInput` | Text input with decimal keyboard hints; `value` stays a raw string. |

## When to use and examples

Do: label Amount (BTC), describe available funds, keep 0,001 unchanged until host validates locale. Don’t: placeholder-only labels, Number(raw) on every keystroke, or strip IME text.

## States, interaction and accessibility

Single-line inputs are 48-unit pills on the surface fill with a subtle border; focus thickens the border to a neutral ring and invalid inputs take the negative border. TextArea keeps a rounded rectangle. DOM label/id plus help/error aria-describedby; invalid state is explicit. Field required propagates to Input/TextArea for browser required semantics and form validation; explicit input props can override required. A disabled Field keeps its controls disabled even if a child requests otherwise. Native amount keyboardType and search returnKeyType remain host-overridable defaults for locale/negative-entry and submit flows. RN visible label plus accessibilityLabel/Hint; errors stay visible and live. Secure input and autofill remain host-controlled native props.

State review: rest; keyboard focus/hover (DOM); accepted press and release/cancel; selected/checked where applicable; disabled; busy; inline error/recovery; empty/loading; long translations/large text; reduced motion; sound and haptics disabled. No host action occurs on mere focus. Disabled/busy targets suppress accepted activation. Core has no required feedback backend; the optional provider callback follows the action, honors cancellation and isolates errors.

## Platform mapping and limits

RN decimal-pad has locale/platform differences; no implicit money parser. Host owns safe area and keyboard avoidance: on Android 15 edge-to-edge (Expo 54) the window no longer resizes for the IME, so wrap scrollable forms in `KeyboardAvoidingView behavior='padding'` on Android and use `automaticallyAdjustKeyboardInsets` on the iOS ScrollView, as the native gallery does. iOS Simulator and Android emulator runs show the AmountInput decimal pad and the focused field kept above the keyboard (`evidence/native-sim/`); physical IME composition and hardware-keyboard behavior remain device observations.

## Validation and citation

See `tests/components.dom.test.tsx`, `tests/native/components.test.cjs`, consumer fixtures and milestone evidence. Physical hardware, assistive-technology and baseline product comparisons are unperformed unless linked explicitly. Cite HIG 0.1.0 with this chapter anchor and a commit permalink, not a mutable preview branch. Preserve business behavior behind a host rollback flag during adoption.


## Financial data · HIG 0.1.0
Source: docs/components/financial-data.md

# Financial data · HIG 0.1.0

Readable numbers, metrics, lists, and tables for host-provided financial data.

Includes `NumberReadout`, `AnimatedNumberReadout`, `Usd`, `Percent`, `Metric`, `Stat`, `Row`, and `List`. `Table` is web-only; native uses labeled lists.

Issue #19. Entry: `data`. Import platform entries from `@bloxwap/hig-react/data` or `@bloxwap/hig-native/data` according to applicability below. Import `@bloxwap/hig-react/css` once on web; tokens CSS is a separate explicit import.

## API and anatomy

| Component | Key props and behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Readouts | `value` accepts a number, `null`, or `undefined`. Locale comes from the provider; `options`, `stale`, and `label` control presentation. |
| `List` | `items`, `keyFor`, `render`, `empty`, `label`, `loading`, `error`, `onRetry`, and `onLoadMore`. |
| `Table` | `caption`, `rows`, `columns`, and `keyFor`; optional host sorting callbacks. |

Loading keeps existing rows visible, suppresses a misleading empty message, and disables pagination and retry until ready. Error text remains visible with an optional host retry action. Native lists use FlatList virtualization; stable host keys preserve identity during live updates.

## When to use and examples

Do: show — for unknown and 0 for zero; mark stale. Don’t: turn a formatted number into order quantity or announce every live tick. Locale display, USD vs USDC, signed PnL and compact notation follow the [localization guide](../foundations/localization.md). Vocabulary follows the [glossary](../foundations/glossary.md).

## States, interaction and accessibility

Readouts are static and tabular, respecting reduced motion. Percent uses percent points (5 is 5%), with localized percent placement/digits and a single native text readout. Intl options control precision/trailing zeros/sign; percent style is enforced. Unknown/nonfinite values stay —. DOM table caption/column headers/aria-sort and scroll region; RN FlatList labeled-row alternative with stable keys.

State review: rest; keyboard focus/hover (DOM); accepted press and release/cancel; selected/checked where applicable; disabled; busy; inline error/recovery; empty/loading; long translations/large text; reduced motion; sound and haptics disabled. No host action occurs on mere focus. Disabled/busy targets suppress accepted activation. Core has no required feedback backend; the optional provider callback follows the action, honors cancellation and isolates errors.

## Platform mapping and limits

Numbers are display-only IEEE numeric inputs, no decimal arithmetic or hidden parser. Exact financial strings remain host-owned. No heavy DataTable engine; optional virtualization/sorting belongs to host. Native list device performance pending.

## Validation and citation

See `tests/components.dom.test.tsx`, `tests/native/components.test.cjs`, consumer fixtures and milestone evidence. Physical hardware, assistive-technology and baseline product comparisons are unperformed unless linked explicitly. Cite HIG 0.1.0 with this chapter anchor and a commit permalink, not a mutable preview branch. Preserve business behavior behind a host rollback flag during adoption.

## Optional number motion

`AnimatedNumberReadout` lives in the separate `animated-number` entry on both platforms. It fades the final localized reading on a deliberate value change, using Web Animations or the RN native opacity driver. It never interpolates financial values or adds a live region. Reduced motion, unknown values and changes less than 250 ms apart use the static final reading; pending motion is canceled on replacement/unmount. No animation engine is imported by the ordinary `data` entry. Example: `import {AnimatedNumberReadout} from '@bloxwap/hig-react/animated-number'` (or `hig-native/animated-number`), then `<AnimatedNumberReadout value={price} label="Price" options={{style:'currency',currency:'USD'}} />`. The same gallery manifest contains runnable examples for both renderers.


## Navigation · HIG 0.1.0
Source: docs/components/navigation.md

# Navigation · HIG 0.1.0

Tabs, disclosure, search, and navigation that keep the current location clear.

Includes `Tabs`, `Accordion`, `Pagination`, `Navigation`, and `Search`. `Breadcrumb` is web-only; native alternatives include `BackButton` and `BottomNavigation`.

Issue #17. Entry: `navigation`. Import platform entries from `@bloxwap/hig-react/navigation` or `@bloxwap/hig-native/navigation` according to applicability below. Import `@bloxwap/hig-react/css` once on web; tokens CSS is a separate explicit import.

## API and anatomy

| Component | Key props and behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `Tabs` | `label`, `items`, `value`, `defaultValue`, and `onValueChange`. Items include panel content and optional `disabled`. |
| `Navigation` | Web links use `href`; native destinations use host callbacks. |
| `Search` | `query`, `results`, `loading`, and `error`. The host supplies the search index and router. |

## When to use and examples

Do: expose current location and keep deep-link ownership with host. Don’t: replace native back with a browser history dependency.

## States, interaction and accessibility

Tabs use selected states and one active panel; DOM Arrow/Home/End keys, RTL-aware arrow mapping. Only the selected tab is in the Tab order. The active DOM panel is a tab stop only when its first content is not focusable. When the panel starts with a focusable element, such as the `InstallCommand` `pre`, that element is the single stop after the tab list. Panels that start with text keep `tabIndex=0` so their content stays reachable. Accordion uses details/summary on DOM and expanded Pressable on RN. Search results are visible action lists; keyboard shortcuts belong to host.

State review: rest; keyboard focus/hover (DOM); accepted press and release/cancel; selected/checked where applicable; disabled; busy; inline error/recovery; empty/loading; long translations/large text; reduced motion; sound and haptics disabled. No host action occurs on mere focus. Disabled/busy targets suppress accepted activation. Core has no required feedback backend; the optional provider callback follows the action, honors cancellation and isolates errors.

## Platform mapping and limits

Breadcrumb is DOM-specific; native host routes plus BackButton are supported alternatives. No fuzzy-search engine, command palette shortcut hijacking or native hardware-keyboard certification.

## Validation and citation

See `tests/components.dom.test.tsx`, `tests/native/components.test.cjs`, consumer fixtures and milestone evidence. Physical hardware, assistive-technology and baseline product comparisons are unperformed unless linked explicitly. Cite HIG 0.1.0 with this chapter anchor and a commit permalink, not a mutable preview branch. Preserve business behavior behind a host rollback flag during adoption.


## Overlays · HIG 0.1.0
Source: docs/components/overlays.md

# Overlays · HIG 0.1.0

Dialogs, sheets, menus, and contextual help with explicit dismissal and focus behavior.

Includes `Dialog`, `AlertDialog`, `Sheet`, and `Menu`. `Popover` and `Tooltip` are web-only; native help uses persistent `HelpText`.

Issue #16. Entry: `overlay`. Import platform entries from `@bloxwap/hig-react/overlay` or `@bloxwap/hig-native/overlay` according to applicability below. Import `@bloxwap/hig-react/css` once on web; tokens CSS is a separate explicit import.

## API and anatomy

| Component | Key props and behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `Dialog` | Controlled `open` and `onOpenChange`, plus `title`, `description`, and `children`. The web `trigger` is one element that accepts a ref. `closeLabel` overrides the Close button (`Sheet`, web `Popover`, native `Menu` and `GestureSheet` too); web `AlertDialog` takes `cancelLabel`. Defaults come from HIGProvider [`messages`](../foundations/localization.md#built-in-component-strings). |
| Native focus targets | `initialFocusRef` and `returnFocusRef` accept live focus targets. Initial focus defaults to the title; the host supplies the trigger ref (Menu and Select pass their own trigger). |
| `Menu` | `label` and items with `label`, optional `disabled`, and `onSelect`. |

Native return focus is scheduled after the static Modal closes and canceled on reopen or unmount.

## When to use and examples

Do: repeat the order amount and give an explicit cancel action. Don’t: hide essential terms in hover help or execute confirm on open.

## States, interaction and accessibility

DOM Radix focus scopes restore trigger focus, trap modal focus, handle Escape and scroll locks. AlertDialog blocks outside-click dismissal. Menus use roving keyboard focus. Native Modal owns back and keyboard avoidance with scrollable content. Native overlays follow the host orientation: React Native's iOS Modal defaults `supportedOrientations` to portrait, so HIG passes every orientation and opening a Dialog, AlertDialog, Sheet, Menu or Select never rotates a landscape host back to portrait (observed on the iOS Simulator, `evidence/native-sim/ios/orientation/`). Hosts still decide which orientations the app supports.

State review: rest; keyboard focus/hover (DOM); accepted press and release/cancel; selected/checked where applicable; disabled; busy; inline error/recovery; empty/loading; long translations/large text; reduced motion; sound and haptics disabled. No host action occurs on mere focus. Disabled/busy targets suppress accepted activation. Core has no required feedback backend; the optional provider callback follows the action, honors cancellation and isolates errors.

## Platform mapping and limits

Basic Sheet uses static Modal layout. The separate optional `@bloxwap/hig-native/gesture-sheet` entry provides GestureSheet with sorted snapPoints, initialIndex, dismissible, safe-area/keyboard configuration, reduced-motion mapping, native back, scoped listener cleanup and controlled dismissal deduplication. Rejected controlled closes re-present after host state settles. See `fixtures/native/gesture-sheet.tsx` and `index-gesture.js` for the real separate consumer; packed smoke compiles both Android/iOS entry points. Hosts provide GestureHandlerRootView, SafeAreaProvider and BottomSheetModalProvider. Required optional peers are Gorhom 5.2.14, Reanimated 4.1.1, Worklets 0.5.1 and Gesture Handler 2.28.0, pinned to Expo 54 bundledNativeModules rather than the newer monorepo native runtime. Backend configuration follows [Gorhom usage](https://gorhom.dev/react-native-bottom-sheet/modal/usage) and [props](https://gorhom.dev/react-native-bottom-sheet/props). Mocked wiring and Metro compilation are not gesture-detent or TalkBack certification. With TalkBack on the Android emulator, opening Dialog/AlertDialog/Sheet/Menu moves accessibility focus to the heading and Back closes the overlay; without a `returnFocusRef` TalkBack falls back to the first screen element, so hosts should pass the trigger. VoiceOver does not run in the iOS Simulator, so VoiceOver focus restoration remains a physical-device observation (`evidence/native-sim/`). Native help is persistent text; no hover tooltip or anchored popover claim.

## Validation and citation

See `tests/components.dom.test.tsx`, `tests/native/components.test.cjs`, consumer fixtures and milestone evidence. Physical hardware, assistive-technology and baseline product comparisons are unperformed unless linked explicitly. Cite HIG 0.1.0 with this chapter anchor and a commit permalink, not a mutable preview branch. Preserve business behavior behind a host rollback flag during adoption.


## Recipes · HIG 0.1.0
Source: docs/components/recipes.md

# Recipes · HIG 0.1.0

Composed patterns for balances, markets, trade review, and documentation.

Includes `MarketRow`, `BalanceCard`, `TradeEntry`, `ActivityList`, `InstallCommand`, `CodeWindow`, and `MarketingHero`.

Issue #26. Entry: `recipes`. Import platform entries from `@bloxwap/hig-react/recipes` or `@bloxwap/hig-native/recipes` according to applicability below. On web, each recipe also has its own entry, for example `@bloxwap/hig-react/recipes/install-command`, `recipes/code-window`, `recipes/market-row`, `recipes/balance-card`, `recipes/marketing-hero` and `recipes/activity-list`. These need no Radix peer; `smoke:packed-boundaries` renders and bundles them with no Radix installed (#63). `recipes/trade-entry` and the aggregate `recipes` entry need `@radix-ui/react-dialog` for the confirm step. Import `@bloxwap/hig-react/css` once on web; tokens CSS is a separate explicit import.

## API and anatomy

All data and actions are supplied by the host application.

| Recipe | Key props and behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `TradeEntry` | Raw `amount`, `onAmountChange`, `onConfirm`, `available`, `busy`, and `error`; opens review before submission. |
| `InstallCommand` | `command` and `onCopy`; accepts an asynchronous host clipboard adapter. |

## When to use and examples

Do: compose primitives and explicit outcomes in comfortable app or compact Pro context. Don’t: put wallet/network/SDK services in core packages.

## States, interaction and accessibility

Native CodeWindow and InstallCommand render code in the provider's `monoFontFamily` (for example the registered `BloxwapMonoRegular`; platform monospace otherwise) and keep code left-to-right inside RTL roots. Copy failures leave a manual-selection recovery message. Trade confirm remains host-controlled; no demo sends a transaction. Web/native fixtures show balance, market, entry and feedback preference previews.

State review: rest; keyboard focus/hover (DOM); accepted press and release/cancel; selected/checked where applicable; disabled; busy; inline error/recovery; empty/loading; long translations/large text; reduced motion; sound and haptics disabled. No host action occurs on mere focus. Disabled/busy targets suppress accepted activation. Core has no required feedback backend; the optional provider callback follows the action, honors cancellation and isolates errors.

## Platform mapping and limits

M2 supplies visual recipes; M3 adds semantic feedback composition because #26 depends on #25. Product visual fidelity is provisional until inaccessible monorepo audit. Account/positions variants can compose these primitives without service coupling.

## Validation and citation

See `tests/components.dom.test.tsx`, `tests/native/components.test.cjs`, consumer fixtures and milestone evidence. Physical hardware, assistive-technology and baseline product comparisons are unperformed unless linked explicitly. Cite HIG 0.1.0 with this chapter anchor and a commit permalink, not a mutable preview branch. Preserve business behavior behind a host rollback flag during adoption.


## Selection controls · HIG 0.1.0
Source: docs/components/selection.md

# Selection controls · HIG 0.1.0

Controls for choosing options, changing preferences, and adjusting values.

Includes `Checkbox`, `RadioGroup`, `Switch`, `SegmentedControl`, `Select`, and `Slider`. See the navigation guide for `Tabs`.

Issue #15. Entry: `selection`. Import platform entries from `@bloxwap/hig-react/selection` or `@bloxwap/hig-native/selection` according to applicability below. Import `@bloxwap/hig-react/css` once on web; tokens CSS is a separate explicit import.

## API and anatomy

| Control | Key props and behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Checkbox and switch | `checked`, `defaultChecked`, and `onCheckedChange`. Native `Switch` also takes `tone`, a token role (`action` default, `positive`, `negative`, `warning`, `info`, `buy`, `sell`) for the on track; raw colours are not accepted and fall back to `action`. On Android the thumb uses the `text` token, so the app theme accent never shows. |
| Choice controls | `value`, `defaultValue`, and `onValueChange`. Options have `value`, `label`, and optional `disabled`. |
| `Slider` | `min`, `max`, `step`, and `value`; a visible `label` is required. The DOM keyboard focus ring is drawn inside the 48px range box, so it never paints over the label or the next control at comfortable or compact density. |

## When to use and examples

Do: control selection from accepted host state. Don’t: emit a success cue on every render or repeated slider value.

## States, interaction and accessibility

Native HTML controls retain browser keyboard and selection semantics. RN Switch renders the OS track inside one labeled 48dp switch row (the row is the accessibility element and touch target); checkbox/radio use labeled Pressables with checked state. RN slider uses the optional community backend for the visual track and touch drag; a plain 48dp adjustable View owns the label, value and increment/decrement actions (5% steps) on iOS and Android because the backend's iOS Fabric view ignores accessibility increments and its Android SeekBar node measures 18dp. On Android the wrapper is the package's autolinked `HIGAdjustableView`, which also lists `ACTION_SET_PROGRESS` for Voice Access and Switch Access: a requested value snaps to `step`, clamps to `min`/`max`, updates the control once and is rejected while disabled. React Native's own `accessibilityActions` cannot express set-progress (custom names get synthetic ids and the progress argument is dropped). Without native linking (Expo Go) the wrapper is a plain View and set-progress is absent. The backend's native track height (18dp Android, 40pt iOS) still bounds direct touch drag; hosts needing a larger drag area should pad around the control. Select opens labeled native Modal choices and returns focus to its trigger.

State review: rest; keyboard focus/hover (DOM); accepted press and release/cancel; selected/checked where applicable; disabled; busy; inline error/recovery; empty/loading; long translations/large text; reduced motion; sound and haptics disabled. No host action occurs on mere focus. Disabled/busy targets suppress accepted activation. Core has no required feedback backend; the optional provider callback follows the action, honors cancellation and isolates errors.

## Platform mapping and limits

SegmentedControl is single-choice radio semantics, not navigation. Native picker alternative is deliberate. Accessibility increment/decrement, set-progress and disabled rejection are verified on the iOS Simulator and Android emulator (`evidence/native-sim/`); tactile drag feel and haptic rate remain physical-device work; backend is an optional native peer.

## Validation and citation

See `tests/components.dom.test.tsx`, `tests/native/components.test.cjs`, consumer fixtures and milestone evidence. Physical hardware, assistive-technology and baseline product comparisons are unperformed unless linked explicitly. Cite HIG 0.1.0 with this chapter anchor and a commit permalink, not a mutable preview branch. Preserve business behavior behind a host rollback flag during adoption.


## Status & feedback · HIG 0.1.0
Source: docs/components/status.md

# Status & feedback · HIG 0.1.0

Visible progress, notifications, and recoverable states that keep people informed.

Includes `Badge`, `Alert`, `Callout`, `Toast`, `Progress`, `Spinner`, `Skeleton`, `EmptyState`, `Avatar`, and `StatusIndicator`.

Issue #18. Entry: `status`. Import platform entries from `@bloxwap/hig-react/status` or `@bloxwap/hig-native/status` according to applicability below. Import `@bloxwap/hig-react/css` once on web; tokens CSS is a separate explicit import.

## API and anatomy

| Component | Key props and behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `Alert` | `title`, `severity`, and an optional recovery `action`. Severity sets the accent edge from a token role on web and native: info → `info`, success → `positive`, warning → `warning`, error → `negative`. On native, `tone` swaps in another token role for an approved product accent, never a raw colour. |
| `Callout` | Same API as `Alert`, for static guidance. It adds the documentation severities `note` (`info` role) and `tip` (`positive` role), so SDK docs do not need their own edge colours. Pass `announce={false}` for callouts present at page load. `title` accepts a ReactNode, such as text with a `<code>` span; on web it renders inside `<strong>` and should stay inline. On native it renders inside the `Heading`, so pass a string or inline `Text`; its visible text is announced. |
| `Toast` | `notices` with stable `id`, `message`, `severity`, and optional `action`; `onDismiss` handles dismissal. `dismissLabel` overrides the visible Dismiss text; the accessible name is `messages.dismissNotice(message, dismissLabel)` and always contains it. |
| `Progress` | `label`, `value`, and `max`. |
| `EmptyState` | `title`, `description`, and an optional `action`. |

## When to use and examples

Do: keep critical failure inline with Retry; use toast for copied acknowledgement. Don’t: dismiss critical text on a timer or rely on audio for success.

## States, interaction and accessibility

Notifications deduplicate ids and preserve every message until explicit dismissal, including bursts larger than three. Host delivery queues may limit arrivals, but the renderer never silently removes an undismissed message. A single coalesced announcement reports each changed burst, prioritizing errors; unchanged rerenders do not repeat it. DOM and Expo web use one live region while every notification remains visible. Native Android uses explicit announcement delivery, and inline Android status uses live-region metadata; iOS announces changed inline content explicitly. Actual VoiceOver/TalkBack timing remains unobserved. Skeleton and spinner are static under candidate motion policy.

State review: rest; keyboard focus/hover (DOM); accepted press and release/cancel; selected/checked where applicable; disabled; busy; inline error/recovery; empty/loading; long translations/large text; reduced motion; sound and haptics disabled. No host action occurs on mere focus. Disabled/busy targets suppress accepted activation. Core has no required feedback backend; the optional provider callback follows the action, honors cancellation and isolates errors.

## Platform mapping and limits

Toast is an inline notification stack, no mandatory portal/timer backend. Host owns delivery ordering/persistence. VoiceOver/TalkBack observations are pending, automated role/state tests are not device evidence.

## Validation and citation

See `tests/components.dom.test.tsx`, `tests/native/components.test.cjs`, consumer fixtures and milestone evidence. Physical hardware, assistive-technology and baseline product comparisons are unperformed unless linked explicitly. Cite HIG 0.1.0 with this chapter anchor and a commit permalink, not a mutable preview branch. Preserve business behavior behind a host rollback flag during adoption.


## Optional adapters and installation · HIG 0.1.0
Source: docs/feedback/adapters.md

# Optional adapters and installation · HIG 0.1.0

Issues #22–#24. Base imports do not load adapters. Individual `web-sound`, `browser-haptic`, `web-haptic`, `native` and `react` entries preserve dependency boundaries. The composite `web` entry needs the Haptic package; sound-only consumers should import `web-sound`.

## Web sound

Install `@bloxwap/hig-feedback@0.1.0 @bloxwap/sfx@0.1.0`. `createWebSoundAdapter()` loads SFX only for enabled requests after an accepted interaction. It calls the documented unlock/play APIs, passes per-call volume and uses the same presets as native. New requests replace pending startup, so delayed loading does not create a backlog. It avoids upstream global enabled/volume stores because HIG preferences are root-scoped. `@bloxwap/sfx/react` owns global preference helpers; using those alongside HIG would create competing preference owners.

The upstream engine is shared and does not expose per-root voice handles. HIG reference-counts its users and disposes the engine after its last default adapter. Muting/cancellation prevents pending playback; it cannot surgically stop an already-running voice for one root. A host that also owns the upstream global engine should inject/own the lifecycle rather than use the default HIG lifecycle. Full per-root active-voice cancellation is an explicit upstream API gap, not a claimed capability. Upstream [sfx#51](https://github.com/bloxwap/sfx/pull/51) adds a per-play `AbortSignal`; HIG adopts it only once it ships in a released `@bloxwap/sfx` (tracked in #70).

## Browser and physical-tap haptics

`createBrowserHapticAdapter()` maps accepted semantic events to browser vibration when `navigator.vibrate` exists. Device intensity/pattern quality varies and may be suppressed. iOS WebKit without vibration cannot provide imperative async outcome feedback; the adapter reports unavailable and remains silent.

For approved iOS physical action targets, install `@bloxwap/haptic@0.1.0` and wrap a single ref-capable HIG button in `HapticFeedbackTarget eligible`. The wrapper uses upstream `HapticTarget`, preserves the target/handler/ref, enables only the physical-tap route and disables debug audio/helper switch visibility. Thus browser vibration comes from the semantic adapter and is not duplicated by the wrapper. HIG preferences still gate the wrapper.

**Do** pre-approve the target with `eligible` after disabled/busy/policy checks. **Don't** wrap an action whose eligibility is decided only by an async click callback, or promise a programmable iOS success/error pattern. The OS physical tick occurs before delegated handlers; a later preventDefault cannot retract that tick. That cancellation limitation, physical-tap intensity limits and device/VoiceOver checks remain upstream [haptic#9](https://github.com/bloxwap/haptic/issues/9) / [haptic#7](https://github.com/bloxwap/haptic/issues/7). The missing imperative iOS API for semantic controllers is [haptic#27](https://github.com/bloxwap/haptic/issues/27) (tracked in #70). No wrapper is required for basic actions.

## Native audio

Install the feedback package plus `expo-audio ~1.1.1` only in the native host setup. `expoAudioBackend(Audio)` supplies a thin playback bridge; `createNativeSoundAdapter(backend, assets)` accepts Metro asset ids. The Expo gallery imports only the four committed WAV cues. Configure ambient/silent-mode behavior with `playsInSilentMode:false`, no background playback and `doNotMix` interruption mode. Host AppState calls `setBackground`; backgrounding pauses cached players. Call `preload()` at startup: it configures the audio session and caches players once. After that, `play()` dispatches synchronously, with no awaited bridge round trip before `player.play()`. It stops only the previous cue, issues `seekTo(0)` without awaiting it (native players apply calls in order) and plays. A cue requested before preload settles waits for it, and only the newest such request plays. Concurrency is limited to one active cue, volume/mute are honored, missing cues are silent, and disposal pauses/removes every cached player.

Regenerate with `npm run generate:cues`. `assets/manifest.json` pins package/recipe/export flags, 48kHz mono PCM16, durations, peaks/RMS, bytes and reviewed hashes. Noise recipes vary; do not assert regenerated WAV bytes are deterministic. Inspect duration/envelope/level tolerances and review the actual artifact hashes. Offline generation dependencies are dev-only; Metro never imports them or browser synthesis.

## Native haptics

Install `expo-haptics ~15.0.7` in the native host. `expoHapticBackend(Haptics)` bridges selection, impact light/medium/heavy and notification success/warning/error. `createNativeHapticAdapter` reports API availability separately from observation. Unsupported hardware, backgrounding, preferences and failed backend calls are no-ops that do not change primary actions. Android notification/impact approximation and OS suppression must be observed on devices before support is certified.

## Simulated lifecycle regression evidence

The Linux tests inject native player and haptic backends. Pending configure/seek requests are superseded by the newest request; cancellation, backgrounding, zero volume and disposal stop pending playback. Failed configuration can retry. Explicit impact intent reaches the native backend even for an otherwise silent press preset. Pause/remove failures cannot prevent other cached players from being released. A dispatch test drives 400 cues through `FeedbackController` with simulated slow bridge calls (configure 60 ms, seek 40 ms). It asserts that every cue reaches `player.play()` inside `emit()` and that p95 stays under one 16 ms frame. The native gallery stamps each emit and logs `dispatch`/`p95` on every play for simulator and emulator runs. These tests establish dispatch/lifecycle behavior, not observed sound, tactile output, acoustic latency (#55) or OS audio-session behavior.

Menu disclosure and dismissal are intentionally silent. Web/native Menu commits emit a single selection intent after the host handler; a host can cancel that effect with the selection event's `preventDefault()`. Native accordion disclosure emits one silent disclosure intent rather than duplicate activation/selection effects. The Linux three-engine fixture also checks switch, range, menu selection and canceled menu actions with injected adapters.


## Semantic feedback · HIG 0.1.0
Source: docs/feedback/contract.md

# Semantic feedback · HIG 0.1.0

Issues #21, #25. Types in `@bloxwap/hig-contracts/feedback` and `@bloxwap/hig-feedback` import without DOM, RN, React, audio, Expo or hardware APIs. Base renderers accept an optional `FeedbackSink`; no provider or feedback backend is required to perform an action.

| Intent | Timing | Sound | Haptic | Cooldown |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| press/release | gesture phases; visual response | silent | none | none |
| cancel | discarded gesture/action; clears pending work | silent | cancel where possible | none |
| activate | accepted button click/keyboard/native press, after host handler | tick | selection | 80ms |
| selection/toggle | accepted state commit, never a render/repeated/rejected value | tick/toggle | selection | 80ms |
| disclosure | accepted open/close | silent | none | 120ms |
| success | host operation completion with stable operation id | success | notification success | 400ms |
| warning | host outcome | silent | notification warning | 400ms |
| error | host operation failure with visual recovery text | error | notification error | 400ms |
| notification | nonessential transient acknowledgement | silent | none | 800ms |

The exported `presets` table is authoritative. Each event has id, source, intent and origin. An async outcome uses the host operation id, not the button's interaction id; an accepted click does not imply order success. Optional native impact overrides map light/medium/heavy; browser physical-tap intensity cannot be programmed. Live price ticks and general navigation are silent.

**Do** emit a success event after the host request resolves, alongside visible success text. **Don't** play a success sound on press-in, for a rejected controlled value, or on every market render. Busy/disabled/suppressed/cancelled events are rejected. Buttons compose the host handler before activation, honor default prevention, preserve refs and block nested activation propagation. Choice controls emit on committed changes only. Sliders use semantic steps and controller cooldown; no effect queue accumulates. A host cancellation before activation suppresses the request; a physical cue already delivered by the OS cannot be recalled.

Preference precedence: host policy may forbid a channel; persisted user choices enable sound/haptics independently; component suppression can disable its request; OS/browser/backend capability decides whether output is attempted. Volume is clamped 0–1. Motion is a separate setting and OS reduced motion remains respected. Defaults are both channels off. No-feedback, sound-only, haptics-only, both, and host-injected adapter configurations use the same actions. Root/local `FeedbackProvider`s hold independent preference/controller state; a nested button emits one request.

Deduplication uses source/id/intent; host stable outcome ids suppress repeated notifications. Cooldowns drop excess requests, never delay primary actions or queue a backlog. Seen/cadence maps are bounded. Exceptions thrown/rejected by backends and storage are caught. Disposal is idempotent and late startup/preload completions cannot revive disposed players. Capability `available` is API routing, while `observed` records actual physical evidence and remains false in this candidate.


## Preferences, preview and device review · HIG 0.1.0
Source: docs/feedback/preferences.md

# Preferences, preview and device review · HIG 0.1.0

`FeedbackProvider` accepts a stable `createController(preferences)` factory and optional storage adapter. `useFeedback` exposes preferences, update, sink and controller. `FeedbackPreferencesControl` is a render-prop control so DOM and RN use their own shipped Switch/Slider instead of importing another platform. Use a stable factory; mount/replay creates fresh adapters and unmount disposes them. React StrictMode lifecycle is tested.

`jsonStorage` supports browser Storage or native AsyncStorage-shaped interfaces. It uses a versioned key; read legacy saved choices explicitly with a host adapter before writing the new key. `migratePreferences` preserves explicit false sound/haptic choices, legacy soundEnabled/hapticsEnabled, clamped volume and independent reducedMotion/motion. Corrupt/missing storage falls back to muted defaults. A delayed saved read cannot overwrite a newer user choice. Storage rejection leaves the live UI usable.

Web and native fixtures include real independent sound, haptics, volume and motion controls, entry/selection/success preview and visible state. The web fixture persists localStorage; the native gallery persists AsyncStorage. Both wire lifecycle background state. Sound and haptic preferences are never encoded in wallet/trade logic. Native gallery sound import/package/Metro success is automated evidence, not audible/tactile observation.

| Platform | Routing | Claimed observation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Desktop Chrome/Firefox/WebKit | Web Audio after gesture; vibration only when API exists | Automated interaction; no hardware assertion |
| iPhone Safari | optional pre-approved physical target; async haptic adapter unavailable | pending physical tap, VoiceOver, settings/OS review |
| Android browser | browser vibration patterns when allowed | pending device output/intensity |
| Native iOS/Android | Expo audio and selection/impact/notification bridges | pending physical output, latency and interruption review |
| Simulator / Jest mocks | API/contract behavior only | never tactile certification |

Device acceptance record must include HIG/package versions, device, OS/browser, date, observer and actual observations: default/muted channels; each independent combination; volume/silent-mode; latency; interruptions; background/foreground; repeated/nested activation; cancelled scroll/drag; disabled/busy; slider repeated values; iOS preset limits; accessibility helper tab/VoiceOver order; visible recovery with feedback off. Attach video/measurements where useful. Reuse upstream haptic certification rather than declaring simulator passes as hardware proof. Owner: HIG and owning app/haptic maintainers, assignment pending; exception expires 2026-11-13.


## Trading glossary · HIG 0.1.0
Source: docs/foundations/glossary.md

# Trading glossary · HIG 0.1.0

Issue #46. Locked before any locale translation. Machine-readable source: `docs/foundations/glossary.json` (also exported as `/hig/glossary.json`). Formatting rules: [localization guide](localization.md).

Translation agents **must** consume the JSON. The rendered page is a view of that source. Do not invent terms, back-port product UI copy, or fill pending locales.

## Locales

| Locale | Status | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `en-US` | approved | Canonical English. HIG defaultEnvironment and authored documentation locale. |
| `es` | todo | No HIG-approved glossary translation. Do not guess. Observed: apps/app/messages/es.json in the product inventory. |
| `fr` | todo | No HIG-approved glossary translation. Do not guess. Observed: apps/app/messages/fr.json in the product inventory. |
| `ko` | todo | No HIG-approved glossary translation. Do not guess. Observed: apps/app/messages/ko.json in the product inventory. |
| `ko-KR` | todo | No HIG-approved glossary translation. Do not guess. Observed: Google Play store-screenshot locale in the product inventory. |
| `zh-CN` | todo | No HIG-approved glossary translation. Do not guess. Observed: apps/app/messages/zh-CN.json in the product inventory. |
| `zh-Hans` | todo | No HIG-approved glossary translation. Do not guess. Observed: App Store screenshot locale in the product inventory. |
| `de-DE` | not a translation locale | HIG Intl number-format fixture only. Not an approved translation locale. |
| `ar-EG` | not a translation locale | HIG Intl percent/numeral fixture only. RTL is a layout direction, not a glossary locale. |

`en-US` is the only approved HIG glossary locale (`defaultEnvironment.locale`). Product message catalogs and store screenshots listed above are inventory observations, not approvals.

## Change process

1. Edit English fields in `docs/foundations/glossary.json` only. Do not hand-edit this Markdown.
2. Run `node scripts/generate-glossary.mjs` (also invoked by docs generation) and commit the JSON and Markdown together.
3. A term is locked when its English definition, usage notes, do/don't examples and `untranslated` flag are reviewed in this repository. Do not start translations before that lock.
4. Promote a pending locale only by setting `status: approved` and supplying `translations[locale]` for **every** term. Incomplete locales stay `todo`.
5. Never guess a translation. Product/marketing strings are not an approved glossary source.
6. Changing a locked definition is a breaking content change for translation agents. Call out term ids in the PR. Tickers, brand names and `untranslatedForms` never enter translation files.
7. `de-DE` and `ar-EG` remain Intl fixtures, not glossary locales.

This chapter blocks locale translation work until the JSON lock is adopted.

## Terms

### Perpetual (perp)

Term id: `perp`. Aliases: `perps`, `perpetual futures`, `perpetual contract`. **Untranslated:** keep the listed short form in every locale. Untranslated forms: `perp`, `perps`.

**Definition:** A derivative that tracks an asset’s price with no fixed expiry. Funding payments help keep the contract aligned with its underlying market. Stocks, commodities, indices and pre-IPO listings on Bloxwap are perps, not ownership of the underlying asset.

**Usage:** Prefer “perp” in dense UI (market row, ticket). Use “perpetual” once in explanatory copy, then the short form. Never imply the trader owns the tracked stock, commodity or token.

**Do:** Label a Bitcoin market “BTC perp”. Say “open a perp position” rather than “buy Bitcoin” when the instrument is a perpetual.

**Don't:** Don’t call a perp a spot purchase, share, or tokenized stock certificate. Don’t invent an expiry date for a perp.

See also: `funding`, `position`, `leverage`.

### Leverage

Term id: `leverage`. Aliases: `lev`. **Untranslated:** no — translate in approved locales.

**Definition:** Position size relative to the margin supporting it. At 10×, 100 USDC of margin supports 1,000 USDC of notional exposure. Leverage magnifies both gains and losses. Market-specific limits are set by Hyperliquid, not by HIG.

**Usage:** Display as a multiplier with the multiplication sign (`10×`), never as a percent (`1000%`). Keep the `×` suffix untranslated. Limits and available leverage are host-supplied.

**Do:** Show selected leverage as `10×` next to size. Repeat the selected leverage on the review step before the host submits.

**Don't:** Don’t write `10x leverage = safe`. Don’t display leverage as `+1000%` or reuse percent styling.

See also: `margin`, `notional`, `liquidation-price`.

### Margin

Term id: `margin`. Aliases: `collateral`, `cross margin`, `isolated margin`. **Untranslated:** no — translate in approved locales. Untranslated forms: `USDC`.

**Definition:** USDC collateral used to open and maintain a leveraged position. If collateral falls below the maintenance requirement, Hyperliquid can liquidate the position. With cross margin, liquidation can consume the whole trading account, not only one position’s margin.

**Usage:** Bloxwap trading collateral is USDC. Say “margin” for trading collateral; do not call it a deposit held by Bloxwap. Isolated vs cross is a host/protocol mode, not a HIG component.

**Do:** Label available collateral “Available margin (USDC)”. Explain that cross margin can consume the trading account, not only the row’s margin.

**Don't:** Don’t call USDC margin a bank deposit or a Bloxwap-custodied balance. Don’t display unknown margin as `0`.

See also: `usdc`, `leverage`, `liquidation-price`, `position`.

### Position

Term id: `position`. Aliases: `open position`, `exposure`. **Untranslated:** no — translate in approved locales.

**Definition:** Open long or short exposure in one market. A position has size, side, margin, leverage, entry, mark, notional, unrealized PnL and an estimated liquidation price. Closing requires a host-submitted order; HIG never executes a trade.

**Usage:** One row per market/side as the host provides. Don’t merge unrelated markets into a single position label. Size stays a raw decimal string in business logic.

**Do:** Title a row “BTC long” with size, leverage and PnL as separate readouts. Keep last-known position data and mark it stale when the host is offline.

**Don't:** Don’t say “position closed” until the host confirms the close fill. Don’t treat a formatted size as the order quantity.

See also: `long`, `short`, `notional`, `pnl`.

### Liquidation price (liq. price)

Term id: `liquidation-price`. Aliases: `liq price`, `liquidation`, `estimated liquidation price`. **Untranslated:** no — translate in approved locales.

**Definition:** The estimated mark price at which the position no longer meets its maintenance margin and Hyperliquid may force-close it. The figure is an estimate; auto-deleveraging can also close positions, including profitable ones.

**Usage:** Always present it as estimated and host-computed. Higher leverage generally leaves less room for an adverse move. Unknown estimates render as —.

**Do:** Label the readout “Est. liquidation price”. Keep the estimate visible next to leverage when the trader changes size.

**Don't:** Don’t call the estimate a guaranteed stop. Don’t omit “estimated” on first display in a risk-critical surface.

See also: `margin`, `leverage`, `stop`.

### Funding

Term id: `funding`. Aliases: `funding rate`, `funding payment`. **Untranslated:** no — translate in approved locales.

**Definition:** Periodic payments between long and short holders of a perpetual that help keep the contract aligned with its underlying market. Positive funding generally means longs pay shorts; negative funding means shorts pay longs. Funding is separate from exchange and builder fees.

**Usage:** Show the rate and the next payment time. Compute from UTC; display in the user’s locale with an explicit time zone. Hyperliquid funding is hourly; the interval is protocol-owned, not a HIG constant to restyle as a calendar expiry.

**Do:** Label “Funding +0.0100% · next 16:00 UTC”. Use a duration countdown (“in 12 min”) rather than a zone-less clock.

**Don't:** Don’t mix funding into the builder-fee line as if it were the same charge. Don’t show a next-funding time without a time zone.

See also: `perp`, `pnl`, `long`, `short`.

### Profit and loss (PnL)

Term id: `pnl`. Aliases: `P&L`, `unrealized PnL`, `realized PnL`, `net PnL`. **Untranslated:** keep the listed short form in every locale. Untranslated forms: `PnL`.

**Definition:** Profit and loss on a position or account. Unrealized PnL marks an open position; realized PnL is locked in after closes. Net figures may include trading fees and available funding; the host must say which components are included.

**Usage:** Keep the abbreviation PnL in every locale. Pair it with a signed, locale-formatted amount. Color is not a substitute for the sign. Zero is `0`, not empty; unknown is —.

**Do:** Show `PnL +$12.34` with `signDisplay: 'exceptZero'`. Name the readout “Unrealized PnL” or “Net PnL” according to host data.

**Don't:** Don’t translate PnL into an unverified local acronym. Don’t announce every live PnL tick to a screen reader.

See also: `position`, `notional`, `funding`.

### Long

Term id: `long`. Aliases: `UP`. **Untranslated:** no — translate in approved locales.

**Definition:** A position that profits if the market price rises. Opening long buys the perp; closing long sells it. Product chrome may label the action UP; the canonical term remains long.

**Usage:** Map UP/DOWN product labels to long/short in copy, APIs and accessibility names. Buy/sell color means direction, never safety. Don’t leave the canonical term untranslated just because the button says UP.

**Do:** Accessible name: “Long BTC”. Visible tap label may stay “UP” where the product uses it. Pair long with a buy-direction token, not a success/destructive intent.

**Don't:** Don’t say “buy Bitcoin” when the action opens a BTC perp long. Don’t use destructive red for every long close.

See also: `short`, `position`, `perp`.

### Short

Term id: `short`. Aliases: `DOWN`. **Untranslated:** no — translate in approved locales.

**Definition:** A position that profits if the market price falls. Opening short sells the perp; closing short buys it back. Product chrome may label the action DOWN; the canonical term remains short.

**Usage:** Same mapping rules as long. Short is a market direction, not a destructive action. Closing a short is not “selling the asset”.

**Do:** Accessible name: “Short ETH”. Visible tap label may stay “DOWN” where the product uses it. State “close short” for an exit, not “buy ETH”.

**Don't:** Don’t describe a short as borrowing stock or delivering the underlying. Don’t treat DOWN as a glossary synonym that replaces short in docs or APIs.

See also: `long`, `position`, `perp`.

### Stop

Term id: `stop`. Aliases: `stop loss`, `stop-loss`, `SL`, `stop order`. **Untranslated:** keep the listed short form in every locale. Untranslated forms: `SL`.

**Definition:** A reduce-risk order that submits a close when the market reaches a trigger the trader set. It is not a guaranteed fill at that price and it is not the protocol liquidation price.

**Usage:** Label the control “Stop”. If a compact badge uses SL, keep SL untranslated and expose “Stop” to assistive technology. Host owns trigger parsing and submission.

**Do:** Place stop beside take profit as optional risk controls on an open position. Confirm the trigger price as a raw string before the host submits.

**Don't:** Don’t present a stop as insurance against liquidation. Don’t reuse the estimated liquidation price as a silent stop.

See also: `take-profit`, `liquidation-price`, `position`.

### Take profit

Term id: `take-profit`. Aliases: `TP`, `take-profit`. **Untranslated:** keep the listed short form in every locale. Untranslated forms: `TP`.

**Definition:** An order that submits a close when the market reaches a favorable trigger the trader set. Like a stop, it is not a guaranteed fill at that price.

**Usage:** Spell “take profit” in sentences. Compact badges may use TP; keep TP untranslated. Pair with stop; neither replaces a review step.

**Do:** Label the field “Take profit”. Show both trigger and current mark so the trader can see distance.

**Don't:** Don’t hide take profit behind an unlabeled TP icon. Don’t treat a take-profit fill as realized until the host confirms it.

See also: `stop`, `pnl`, `position`.

### Notional

Term id: `notional`. Aliases: `notional value`, `position value`. **Untranslated:** no — translate in approved locales.

**Definition:** Absolute position value in quote terms, typically mark × size. Notional is the exposure, not the margin posted. At 10×, 100 USDC margin corresponds to 1,000 USDC notional.

**Usage:** Use “notional” in Pro/details; “position value” is allowed in first-run copy if it still means mark × size. Never display notional as if it were withdrawable balance.

**Do:** Show “Notional 1,000.00 USDC” separately from “Margin 100.00 USDC”. Keep notional host-computed; HIG only formats the number.

**Don't:** Don’t label margin as notional or notional as available cash. Don’t round notional for display and feed that figure back into an order.

See also: `leverage`, `margin`, `position`.

### Builder fee

Term id: `builder-fee`. Aliases: `builder-fee`, `interface fee`. **Untranslated:** no — translate in approved locales. Untranslated forms: `bps`.

**Definition:** A fee added by an interface that routes orders to Hyperliquid, charged on each fill in addition to the exchange fee. Live rates, Genesis discounts and rebate math belong to the host fee schedule, not this glossary.

**Usage:** Spell “builder fee”. Quote basis points as `bps` (untranslated) with a percent companion (`5 bps (0.05%)`) when showing a rate. Fees apply on open and close fills; funding is separate.

**Do:** Itemize “Builder fee” and “Exchange fee” on the review step. Point at the host fee schedule for the current rate rather than hard-coding it in a component.

**Don't:** Don’t call the builder fee a spread, a spread markup, or Hyperliquid’s exchange fee. Don’t bake a candidate rate into HIG component copy.

See also: `funding`, `pnl`.

### USDC

Term id: `usdc`. Aliases: `USD Coin`. **Untranslated:** yes — keep English. Untranslated forms: `USDC`.

**Definition:** A stablecoin designed to track the US dollar. Bloxwap uses USDC for trading collateral and settlement. It is not the same ticker as USD for display purposes.

**Usage:** Always keep `USDC` untranslated. Format the amount with the locale’s decimal/grouping rules, then place the ticker `USDC` — never a `$` or `currency: 'USD'` style. See the localization guide.

**Do:** Display `1,234.50 USDC`. Use the Usd readout only for actual USD, not for USDC collateral.

**Don't:** Don’t localize USDC to “USD”, “US$”, or a local currency name. Don’t pass `currency: 'USDC'` to Intl; it is not a reliable ISO 4217 code.

See also: `margin`, `notional`, `pnl`.


## Numbers, currency, dates and built-in strings · HIG 0.1.0
Source: docs/foundations/localization.md

# Numbers, currency, dates and built-in strings · HIG 0.1.0

Issue #47. Vocabulary is locked in the [trading glossary](glossary.md); agents consume [`docs/foundations/glossary.json`](glossary.json). Machine-readable format profiles: [`docs/foundations/localization.json`](localization.json). Host owns locale selection, parsing and time zone; HIG formats display only.

`HIGProvider` locale is a BCP 47 tag (`en-US` default). Direction (`ltr`/`rtl`) is independent. `de-DE` and `ar-EG` are Intl fixtures already covered by tests, not approved translation locales.

## Shared helpers

Use the display helpers from `@bloxwap/hig-contracts` and the data readouts. Do not hand-roll separators, currency symbols, compact suffixes, the leverage `×` or zone labels. Every helper returns `—` for `null`, `undefined` and non-finite input.

```ts
import {formatNumber, formatLeverage, formatTicker, formatZonedTime} from '@bloxwap/hig-contracts';
formatNumber(value, locale, options);             // Intl.NumberFormat
formatLeverage(10, locale);                        // '10×' (decimal style forced)
formatTicker(12.34, 'USDC', locale, {signDisplay: 'exceptZero'}); // '+12.34 USDC' (no-break space)
formatZonedTime(instant, locale, 'UTC');           // '4:00 PM UTC' / '16:00 UTC'
```

| Need | API |
| --- | --- |
| Decimal/grouped numbers | `formatNumber` / `NumberReadout` + host `minimumFractionDigits`/`maximumFractionDigits` |
| USD | `Usd` (`style:'currency', currency:'USD'`) |
| USDC | `formatTicker(amount, 'USDC', locale, options)` — decimal amount plus untranslated ticker, never `$` |
| Leverage | `formatLeverage(value, locale)` — `10×`, never percent |
| Percent points | `Percent` (5 means 5%; do not pass a ratio) |
| Signed PnL | `signDisplay:'exceptZero'` on `Usd`/`formatNumber`/`formatTicker` |
| Compact totals | `notation:'compact', compactDisplay:'short'` |
| Funding / expiry clocks | `formatZonedTime(instant, locale, timeZone)` — `Intl.DateTimeFormat` with the zone name always shown |
| Other dates | `Intl.DateTimeFormat` |
| Funding countdown | `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` on a duration, not a zone-less clock |

Hermes in RN 0.81.5 provides `Intl`. Don’t polyfill, don’t concatenate `'$'+value`, and don’t parse a formatted string back into an order.

## Numbers

Grouping and decimal marks come from the locale: `1,234.5` in `en-US`, `1.234,5` in `de-DE`, Eastern Arabic numerals in `ar-EG`. Precision is host-supplied (tick size, `szDecimals`). Generic USD balances may use 2 fraction digits; prices, sizes, funding rates and fees do not share one precision table.

**Do** keep `0` for zero and — for unknown/non-finite; mark stale. **Don’t** use a rounded display value as transaction input, strip unfamiliar separators, or replace Eastern Arabic digits with Latin ones unless a dual readout is explicit.

## Currency, signed PnL and compact notation

USD uses ISO `currency:'USD'`. Intl places the symbol (`$1,234.50` vs `1.234,50 $`). USDC is a ticker, not a reliable ISO 4217 code: use `formatTicker(amount, 'USDC', locale)`, which formats the number without `style:'currency'` and appends `USDC` after a no-break space. Never show USDC as `$` or `USD`.

Signed PnL always includes a sign except at zero (`+$12.34`, `-$12.34`). Color is not a substitute for the sign. Don’t use accounting parentheses.

Compact notation is locale-owned. `1.2K` / `3.4M` is the `en-US` short form; `de-DE` yields `3,4 Mio.`, `ja-JP` may use `万`. Never hard-code `K`/`M`. Compact is for overview totals, not order tickets or review amounts.

USDC PnL follows the same sign rule: `+12.34 USDC`. Tabular nums on every readout.

## Dates, times and funding

`en-US` clocks are 12-hour (`4:00 PM`). Many other locales resolve `h23`. Use `Intl.DateTimeFormat` (`hourCycle` from the locale unless the host overrides). Store instants in UTC.

Funding and expiries: compute the next payment from UTC (Hyperliquid funding is hourly; the interval is protocol-owned). Display the instant with an explicit zone (`16:00 UTC` or a named device zone) using `formatZonedTime`. Pair a duration countdown (“in 12 min”) with that labeled clock. Perps have no expiry — don’t render an expiry field on a perp.

**Don’t** show a funding time without a zone or treat a local wall clock as UTC.

## Leverage and percentages

Leverage is a multiplier with the untranslated `×` suffix (`10×`, via `formatLeverage`), never `1000%` or percent styling. Percentages use the glossary’s rate terms (funding, builder fee as `5 bps (0.05%)`) and `Percent` for percent-point values (`+2.5%`, `-2.5%`). Keep `bps` untranslated.

## RTL and text expansion

Logical inline spacing, wrapping labels, no fixed-height clipping of translated text, Dynamic Type stays on. Plan for ~30–40% expansion (German/Finnish) and 200% text. Directional arrows mirror in RTL; brand, check marks and financial direction (`+`/`−`, buy/sell) do not. Preserve bidi isolates that Intl inserts around signed currency in Arabic. Mixed-script punctuation needs the required font scripts; a Latin-only fixture does not certify them.

Long translations, Arabic/Hebrew RTL and large text remain part of the [platform checklist](platform.md#accessibility-and-localization-10). Physical-device observations are still pending.

## Built-in component strings

Issue #62. HIG components render a small amount of their own copy: the Close button on overlays, the Toast Dismiss button, the Button busy suffix, loading and empty states, and the recipe labels. None of it is hard-coded in `packages/react/src` or `packages/native/src`. Every string comes from a typed `HIGMessages` catalog (`@bloxwap/hig-contracts/messages`). Hosts translate it through `HIGProvider messages`. A few components also take a per-instance prop (`closeLabel`, `cancelLabel`, `dismissLabel`, `busyLabel`).

HIG ships the English (`en-US`) defaults only (`defaultMessages`). It does not ship or guess translations. The host's message catalog owns French, Korean and other copy, under the same rule as the [glossary](glossary.md): an unapproved locale is never filled by guessing.

```tsx
import {HIGProvider} from '@bloxwap/hig-react/provider'; // or '@bloxwap/hig-native/provider'
import type {HIGMessages} from '@bloxwap/hig-contracts/messages';

const fr: Partial<HIGMessages> = {
  close: t('hig.close'),             // from the host catalog, e.g. 'Fermer'
  dismiss: t('hig.dismiss'),
  dismissNotice: (message, dismiss) => `${dismiss} : ${message}`,
  busy: t('hig.busy'),
};

<HIGProvider locale='fr-FR' messages={fr}>…</HIGProvider>
<Dialog closeLabel={t('checkout.back')} …/>   // one instance
<Button busy busyLabel=''>…</Button>           // no visible suffix; busy state stays exposed
```

Resolution order, per key: the component prop, then the nearest `HIGProvider messages`, then any enclosing `HIGProvider messages`, then English. A nested provider for density or direction keeps the host's translations. `undefined` keys and values of the wrong type (a string where a function is expected, or the reverse) are ignored, so a partial catalog never blanks a label. `useMessages()` returns the complete resolved catalog; `useHIG().messages` holds only the host overrides. Each English default is also a named export of `@bloxwap/hig-contracts/messages`, and a component falls back per key (`messages.close ?? en.close`), so importing one component bundles only the copy it renders.

Rules:

- **Visible text and accessible names come from the same key.** The Close, Dismiss and busy text is the button content, so it is also the accessible name. The Toast dismiss name is `dismissNotice(message, dismiss)`. A translation must keep the `dismiss` argument in it, so voice-control users can say the label they see. `stale` and `required` are appended to both the visible text and the accessible name.
- **Close means dismissing an overlay.** `close` closes a dialog or sheet. It is not the glossary sense of closing a position (an exit order). Translate it with the platform's dismiss word, never with the trading term for closing a position.
- **Functions receive formatted arguments.** `pageOf` and `progressValue` receive numbers already formatted for the provider locale (Eastern Arabic digits in `ar-EG`). `resultCount` receives the raw count and the locale, so it can pick a plural form with `Intl.PluralRules`. Translations may reorder arguments. Component code never concatenates words.
- **RTL is a direction, not a translation.** Messages render inside the provider's `dir` (web) or `writingDirection` (native). The Unicode bidi algorithm places the ` · ` busy separator and parentheses. Do not add direction marks to messages.
- **Trading words stay with the host.** Default messages contain no glossary term. The TradeEntry recipe copy (`reviewAssetOrder`, `confirmOrder`, …) is generic order-review copy. The host supplies the asset ticker, which stays untranslated.

| Key | English default | Where | Prop override |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `close` | Close | Dialog, Sheet, Popover (web), Menu and GestureSheet (native) close button | `closeLabel` |
| `cancel` | Cancel | AlertDialog (web) decline button | `cancelLabel` |
| `dismiss` | Dismiss | Toast dismiss button text | `dismissLabel` |
| `dismissNotice` `(message, dismiss)` | {dismiss} {message} | Toast dismiss accessible name; must contain the `dismiss` argument | — |
| `busy` | Working | Button busy suffix, shown as ` · {busy}`; `''` hides it | `busyLabel` |
| `notifications` | Notifications | Toast region name (web) | — |
| `loading` | Loading | Spinner label (web appends `…`) | `label` |
| `loadingContent` | Loading content | Skeleton label | `label` |
| `loadingItems` | Loading items | List loading row | — |
| `loadingChart` | Loading chart… | PriceChart fallback (web) | — |
| `noItems` | No items | List empty text | `empty` |
| `noRows` | No rows | Table empty text (web) | — |
| `retry` | Retry | List retry button | — |
| `loadMore` | Load more | List load-more button | — |
| `stale` | (stale) | NumberReadout stale marker (visible and accessible) | — |
| `required` | (required) | Field required marker (visible and accessible) | — |
| `breadcrumb` | Breadcrumb | Breadcrumb landmark name (web) | — |
| `pagination` | Pagination | Pagination landmark name (web) | — |
| `previous` | Previous | Pagination previous button | — |
| `next` | Next | Pagination next button | — |
| `pageOf` `(page, total)` | Page {page} of {total} | Pagination position; numbers arrive locale-formatted | — |
| `search` | Search | Search field label | — |
| `searching` | Searching… | Search in-progress status | — |
| `noResults` | No results | Search empty status | — |
| `resultCount` `(count, locale)` | {count} result / {count} results | Search result count (native); use `Intl.PluralRules` for other plural forms | — |
| `back` | Back | BackButton (native) | — |
| `menuDescription` | Available actions | Menu sheet description (native) | — |
| `choose` | Choose | Select trigger before a choice (native) | — |
| `chooseOne` | Choose one option. | Select sheet description (native) | — |
| `inProgress` | In progress | Indeterminate Progress value text (native) | — |
| `progressValue` `(value, max)` | {value} of {max} | Determinate Progress value text (native); numbers arrive locale-formatted | — |
| `copied` | Copied | InstallCommand success status | — |
| `copyFailed` | Copy failed. Select the command and copy manually. | InstallCommand failure status | — |
| `copyInstallCommand` | Copy install command | InstallCommand button | — |
| `reviewAssetOrder` `(asset)` | Review {asset} order | TradeEntry heading | — |
| `amountInAsset` `(asset)` | Amount ({asset}) | TradeEntry amount label | — |
| `availableAmount` `(available)` | Available: {available} | TradeEntry amount description | — |
| `reviewOrder` | Review order | TradeEntry review button | — |
| `confirmOrder` | Confirm order | TradeEntry dialog title and confirm button | — |
| `confirmOrderDescription` `(amount, asset)` | Amount: {amount} {asset}. Verify the host-provided terms before submission. | TradeEntry dialog description | — |
| `orderUnavailable` | Order unavailable | TradeEntry error title (web) | — |
| `noActivity` | No activity yet | ActivityList empty text | — |
| `statusOnline` | online | StatusIndicator `online` | — |
| `statusOffline` | offline | StatusIndicator `offline` | — |
| `statusStale` | stale | StatusIndicator `stale` | — |

`npm run lint` runs `scripts/check-built-in-strings.mjs`, and so does `tests/built-in-strings.test.ts`. The check fails when a component under `packages/{react,native}/src` adds a user-visible or accessible literal. That covers JSX text, a visible or accessibility attribute (`aria-label`, `accessibilityLabel`, `title`, `label`, `description`, …), a label-like default prop and a `set…()` status string. To add copy, add a key to `HIGMessages`, read it with `useMessages()`, and add a row to the table above. The test checks that every key is in this table with its English default.

## Validation

See `tests/tokens.test.ts`, `tests/data.dom.test.tsx`, `tests/glossary.test.ts`, `tests/built-in-strings.test.ts`, `tests/messages.dom.test.tsx`, `tests/native/messages.test.cjs`, `docs/foundations/localization.json` and the data chapter. Cite HIG 0.1.0 with this chapter anchor and a commit permalink.


## Foundation and platform rules · HIG 0.1.0
Source: docs/foundations/platform.md

# Foundation and platform rules · HIG 0.1.0

## Color (#6)

Dark is the only audited mode. Source values retain the commit-pinned monorepo authored OKLCH and brand channels; see [source reconciliation](source-reconciliation.md).
