Use surface/text/action/focus/buy/sell/warning roles, never infer intent from a hue. Web emits sRGB then P3 in `@supports`. RN uses explicit hex values; iOS Display-P3 hosts use the generated iosDisplayP3 channel hex map; hosts using sRGB retain ios/Android values. Android and third-party images use sRGB. `evidence/contrast.json` records all 33 approved normal-text pairings. Faint text is restricted to background/surface: faint on nested fails normal-text AA, so use muted on nested instead. Border is decorative; meaningful control edges/focus must use tested text or focus tones. **Do** use onAction on green fills; **don't** put white body text on green.

## Typography (#7)

Pin @bloxwap/font 0.1.2. Vite: import `@bloxwap/font/css`; Next: upstream Sans/Mono loaders own loading and script fallback. Sans for prose/controls; Mono for code and tabular readouts; Pixel for a short nonessential accent. Body 16/24, label 14/20, caption 12/18, title 24/30, display 48/52 are candidate role mappings based on SDK scale. Web CSS exposes the roles as `--hig-type-<role>-size`, `-line-height`, `-weight` and a `--hig-type-<role>` font shorthand, and the families as `--hig-font-sans`/`--hig-font-mono`. Those resolve the `@bloxwap/font` Next loader variables first and fall back to the literal `'Bloxwap Sans'`/`'Bloxwap Mono'` families, so HIG controls render the loaded face in both Next and plain `@font-face` hosts. Web rem uses 16px root; RN sizes are explicit dp and allow font scaling. Do not disable Dynamic Type or fixed-height clip translated labels. Run the pinned native font generator and register its static TTF faces from `@bloxwap/hig-native-fonts`; its typed manifest records weight/family/source hashes. Web hosts never install that package. Published WOFF2/Next loaders are not directly native assets. **Do** wait for registration before applying a custom native family; **don't** invent a family string and claim the font rendered. Arabic/Hebrew/CJK companions are owned upstream; load required scripts, test mixed-script punctuation and RTL. Large-text and device font evidence is pending.

## Geometry and layout (#8)

Spaces 4/8/12/16/20/24/32/48; radius 6/8/10/14 and pill (`--hig-radius-sm`…`--hig-radius-xl`, `--hig-radius-pill`). Comfortable control/target 48 and gap 12; compact 36 and gap 8, reserved for pointer/keyboard dense layouts. CSS exposes each mode as `--hig-density-<mode>-<control|target|gap>`, and `--hig-density-control`, `--hig-density-target` and `--hig-density-gap` follow the nearest `[data-hig-density]`, which the React provider sets. Painted icons can be 16/20/24 while targets stay 48 on touch. Never expand adjacent invisible hit areas so they overlap. Use logical inline spacing, wrapping labels, safe-area insets, keyboard avoidance and a scrollable native sheet; preserve portrait/tablet rotation without locking orientation. Pro tables may scroll with column headers; app amount entry reflows. Elevation uses nested fills rather than unverified shadows. Layer order: document, sticky nav, contextual popover, modal, notification. Browser top layer handles modal stacking; native Modal remains platform-owned.

## Motion and gestures (#9)

Fast 180ms, base 260ms, slow 320ms; web easing `cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1)`. CSS exposes `--hig-motion-duration-<fast|base|slow>` and `--hig-motion-easing-standard`. The durations become 0ms under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` and inside `[data-hig-motion='reduced']`, which the React provider sets when the host or OS asks for reduced motion. Press response ends on release/cancel; action executes on accepted activation, never press-in. Drag/scroll cancellation clears visual and feedback state. Interrupt transitions from current state instead of queuing. Reduced motion uses immediate state changes, static skeletons and unanimated numeric readouts. Outcome messages remain explicit. **Do** animate deliberate disclosure once; **don't** animate or play sound for every live-data update. Native candidate uses static transitions until cancellation/device animation evidence exists; motion preference is independent from sound/haptics.

## Accessibility and localization (#10)

Baseline: [WCAG 2.2 AA, Recommendation 12 December 2024](https://www.w3.org/TR/2024/REC-WCAG22-20241212/). Normal text 4.5:1; large text and meaningful non-text UI 3:1. Touch baseline 48 logical units exceeds the web minimum. Provide visible focus, semantic labels/descriptions, logical keyboard order and non-drag alternatives. Native roles/state/value map to VoiceOver/TalkBack. No tooltip-only critical text. Restore trigger focus on modal dismissal; Escape/native back closes topmost cancellable overlay. Host owns safe-area, locale, parsing, route and keyboard adapters. Intl display is not money arithmetic. Vocabulary is locked in the [trading glossary](glossary.md) (`docs/foundations/glossary.json`) before any locale translation. Number, currency, date, leverage, percent and RTL formatting is in the [localization guide](localization.md).

Component review checklist: keyboard completion; labeled controls/errors; busy/disabled; focus restoration; narrow viewport; 200% text; long translations; Arabic/Hebrew RTL; mixed scripts; reduced motion; sound off; haptics off; unknown/stale/error values; VoiceOver/TalkBack on physical devices. Automated results and physical observations must be separate. Exception requires owner, affected surface, reason, alternative and expiry. No observed device evidence means pending, never pass.

## Brand and icons (#11)

Approved mark is copied verbatim from the pinned Font docs SVG, including embedded provenance. Import `@bloxwap/hig-tokens/mark.svg` on web; both web and RN geometry renderers are available from their brand entries. Keep aspect ratio and clear space of one quarter mark width. Decorative marks/icons are hidden from accessibility; icon-only actions require an explicit accessible name and 48-unit target. Use currentColor for utility icons, never tint the approved brand mark arbitrarily. Directional arrows mirror in RTL; brand, check and financial direction do not. Icons repository contains a large catalog; do not import it wholesale. Only reviewed single glyphs belong in runtime exports. Favicon/OG derivatives have source provenance and drift checks. Physical device visual comparison remains unperformed.

Font-loading note: `@bloxwap/font/css` references all supported families/scripts, which may increase deployed asset bytes even with on-demand browser loading. The Latin web fixture instead uses two explicit @font-face rules with package asset URLs (Sans and Mono). Add only the scripts/italics used by each consumer. Do not assume a Latin-only fixture certifies mixed-script rendering.


## Principles and content · HIG 0.1.0
Source: docs/foundations/principles.md

# Principles and content · HIG 0.1.0

Issues #2, #3. Rules are candidate guidance anchored to SDK source and the public marketing surface; the pinned monorepo audit and live-origin snapshots are in `evidence/issue-1-18/`. Do not represent example trading actions as live product behavior.

## Clear action hierarchy

Offer one primary action per decision. In an amount-entry recipe, **do** label the next step “Review order” and show the asset and amount before host submission; **don't** say “Go” or execute a trade when a field receives focus. Secondary actions navigate or cancel. Destructive intent means irreversible removal/cancellation; buy/sell colors mean market direction and never imply safety. Bind pending state to the host request, block duplicate activation, retain a progress label. Disabled means unavailable; busy means an action is running. Give the reason nearby.

## Touch before density

Use comfortable 48-unit controls for mobile trade forms. **Do** stack amount, available balance, validation and primary action at narrow widths; **don't** squeeze a desktop order panel into a phone. Pro can use compact 36-unit controls with keyboard focus and separated targets. SDK code windows scroll horizontally; surrounding prose reflows. Marketing CTA and SDK install controls retain explicit labels, as observed in `bloxwap.com` and `font/apps/docs/app/global.css`.

## State tells the truth

Resting, hover, focus, pressed, selected, busy, disabled, empty, error, success, offline and stale are distinct states. **Do** retain the last value with a timestamp and “Data unavailable — retry”; **don't** display unknown as zero, silently imply a completed order, or announce every price tick. Errors name the failed action and recovery. Confirmations repeat host-provided consequences and offer cancel before commit. Essential information remains visible and accessible with feedback muted.

## Content and precision

Use sentence case and concrete verbs (“Copy install command”). **Do** display currency, precision and units supplied by the host; **don't** use a rounded display number as transaction input. Keep raw decimal strings in business logic. A percent component expects percent points, not an implicit ratio. Use localized display with explicit parsing policy; do not strip unfamiliar separators and submit a changed amount. Code uses Mono, body Sans, Pixel only as a decorative brand accent.

## Composition and progressive disclosure

Show common actions first, advanced options on deliberate disclosure. **Do** give a native sheet a visible close action and let Android back dismiss; **don't** rely on hover tooltips on touch. Navigation remains host-owned: HIG does not choose routes, wallets, order types, or trading outcomes. Use status/callout for persistent critical errors; toast only for nonessential acknowledgements.

## Concrete source and pattern references

The preceding rules map to Bloxwap-owned examples, without treating host demo outcomes as submitted trades:

- Clear action hierarchy: [pinned Bloxwap source](https://github.com/bloxwap/monorepo/blob/d47cef4c40363184bdfda8d8c263ead108ef9ff6/packages/ui-native/src/components/button.tsx), [HIG pattern](../components/actions-surfaces.md). Source primary/secondary/destructive variants, busy activation policy and semibold labels.
- Touch before density: [pinned Bloxwap source](https://github.com/bloxwap/monorepo/blob/d47cef4c40363184bdfda8d8c263ead108ef9ff6/packages/tokens/src/spacing.ts), [HIG pattern](../components/recipes.md). Source spacing aliases and 16-unit root; marketing CTA before-capture is before-bloxwap.com.png.
- State tells the truth: [pinned Bloxwap source](https://github.com/bloxwap/monorepo/blob/d47cef4c40363184bdfda8d8c263ead108ef9ff6/packages/ui-native/src/components/toast.tsx), [HIG pattern](../components/status.md). Source notification severity and persistent readable outcomes; HIG preserves undismissed bursts.
- Content and precision: [pinned Bloxwap source](https://github.com/bloxwap/monorepo/blob/d47cef4c40363184bdfda8d8c263ead108ef9ff6/packages/ui-native/src/components/number-format.ts), [HIG pattern](../components/fields.md). Source display formatting stays separate from raw amount input and host arithmetic.
- Composition and progressive disclosure: [pinned Bloxwap source](https://github.com/bloxwap/monorepo/blob/d47cef4c40363184bdfda8d8c263ead108ef9ff6/packages/ui-native/src/components/sheet.tsx), [HIG pattern](../components/overlays.md). Source back/dismissal and safe-area behavior; basic HIG Modal alternative has an explicit close action.


## Pinned source reconciliation · HIG 0.1.0
Source: docs/foundations/source-reconciliation.md

# Pinned source reconciliation · HIG 0.1.0

Issues #2, #6–#9, #11–#18. See `evidence/issue-1-18/monorepo-sha.txt` for the exact monorepo commit and `monorepo-source-fetch.json` for all 129 audited paths. This supersedes the earlier 404 source-access limitation; it does not turn old unperformed product/device checks into passes.

The audit covers tokens, shared web/native primitives, plain-ui and app/Pro-owned controls. `monorepo-audit.json` records byte-identical duplicate groups, source bytes, repository asset totals and explicit source component dispositions. The existing catalog/platform matrix defines the HIG destination families. The authenticated organization inventory now includes monorepo, .github-private, taptradetv and tapsiren; their complete observed trees and explicit applicability decisions are recorded in new-repositories.json and planning/adoption.json. Named owner approval remains an organizational blocker, not a fabricated assignment. Confetti, signal strength, animated number backends and overlay layering internals stay optional host integrations; they are not silently added to base imports. Migration owners remain the owning product teams; HIG cannot claim their source forks have been deleted.

## Tokens and platform units

`packages/tokens/upstream-palette.json` preserves the complete authored semantic OKLCH palette and brand sRGB/P3 channels. `sourceColors` exports web strings plus converted Android sRGB and iOS Display-P3 channel values; generated CSS exposes authored `--hig-source-*` variables. The HIG surface, nested, text and muted roles now retain their corresponding authored OKLCH values and tested sRGB fallback. Brand green and blue preserve upstream P3 channels. HIG focus green, market sell red, warning gold, opaque border and faint text are intentional intent/accessibility mappings rather than mislabeled exact source copies; direction remains distinct from destructive intent.

Native views default to sRGB and use `nativeColors.android`/`ios`. A host that explicitly configures RN iOS default color space as Display-P3 must use `nativeColors.iosDisplayP3` throughout, including converted third-party sRGB assets. Never send CSS functions to native views or use P3 channel hex in an sRGB host. These are mathematical conversion checks, not physical wide-gamut display certification.

Source `spacing.ts` and `type.ts` explicitly set both rem roots to 16; native spacing md=12 and base type=16 match HIG. Radius 6/8/10/14 and motion 180/260/320 ms also match. HIG caption line-height 18, title 30 and display 52 intentionally provide readable role leading versus the stock utility steps. Comfortable 48-unit native targets and compact 36-pixel desktop targets remain distinct; compact native buttons still retain 48-unit hit targets. Source native sheets use optional Gorhom/Reanimated gesture backends, 320 ms card transitions and separate 500 ms opening motion. HIG's basic Sheet stays a static, scrollable Modal alternative. The isolated gesture-sheet entry now supplies an optional Gorhom adapter with detents, cancellation delegation, native back, safe-area/keyboard configuration, reduced-motion mapping and focus requests. Its mocked lifecycle and real Metro imports are software-verified; actual worklet, pan interruption and assistive-technology behavior still require a booted native target.

## Native font generation and registration

Install `fonttools[woff]==4.61.1` and `brotli==1.2.0`, then run `npm run generate:fonts` before native consumer commands. `scripts/generate-native-fonts.py` derives static faces exclusively from the installed `@bloxwap/font@0.1.2` variable WOFF2 files, verifying all four input hashes before writing. It adapts the monorepo's generator and preserves its naming/weight metadata. The generated manifest contains input/output SHA256, PostScript names, Expo registration keys, weights, scripts and byte counts; OFL attribution ships beside the faces. Generated TTF files are build outputs, not per-repository committed binary copies. Local tarballs include them through `@bloxwap/hig-native-fonts/fonts/*` (moved out of the web tokens package in #64); consumers register only needed faces.

The Expo fixture registers Sans Regular/SemiBold and Mono Regular through `expo-font`, waits for loading, exposes failure visibly and passes explicit 400/600 family keys to the native provider. Text, headings and buttons select registered static weight families, avoiding an invalid variable family name or synthesized weight. Expo web uses feedback.web.ts browser adapters; Android/iOS retain the native backend. Korean/Simplified Chinese Regular/SemiBold faces can be registered by host locale policy; other scripts use an explicit host/system fallback. Pixel remains a scoped web accent, not a native body-font requirement. Font registration in Expo web and Metro builds does not certify native rasterization, native Dynamic Type, or multilingual physical-device layout.

## Observation boundaries

Headless browser synthetic composition checks preserve raw negative/decimal locale strings without formatting or precision loss; real on-screen IME composition is a separate device check. Browser 200% root text, narrow width and RTL checks exercise DOM reflow, not OS text scaling. Jest inspects RN roles, states and handlers with native modules mocked; Expo web exercises RN web rendering; neither is TalkBack. Android emulator installation, startup and any observed OS semantics are reported separately in `evidence/issue-1-18/`. Physical iOS/Android, tactile output and real VoiceOver/TalkBack observations remain unperformed on this Linux VM.

The root build now compiles contracts/tokens before feedback and platform renderers, so clean builds cannot rely on stale dist output. The expanded browser flow runs in Chromium/Firefox/WebKit under 320-pixel width, translated RTL tabs and 200% root text. It checks required validation, synthetic composition/raw precision, keyboard range/radio/menu/search, nested focus restoration, persistence/retry and zero automated axe WCAG findings. The Expo-web gallery separately checks registered faces, Modal picker, labels and range keyboard values. The native Slider web backend needs explicit ARIA min/max/now and keyboard actions; native OS builds retain adjustable role/state/value semantics. Checkbox/radio/tab web aliases likewise preserve native-renderer state in RN web. None of these observations is labeled as TalkBack. Quality gates verify every generated native face hash and cap the three selected fixture faces at 1.4 MB; optional CJK/other weight faces are available but are not imported by the default fixture.

# Organization adoption and governance (#36)

- applicability
- owner (a maintainer role until #57 records named owners)
- HIG version
- merged and open PRs
- validation
- status
- remaining work
- dated exceptions, each with scope, reason, owner, an expiry no more than 180 days ahead, and a tracking issue

`tests/docs.test.ts` fails when a visible repository has no row or when a row is missing these fields. Product surfaces (bloxwap.app, bloxwap.pro, bloxwap.com, the React Native app) and the five SDK docs sites have their own rows under `surfaces`.

## Governance

- **Ownership, review, admission, removal, platform support and product exceptions:** see the contribution chapter (`docs/governance/contributing.md`).
- **Release, semver and deprecation:** see the release chapter (`docs/governance/release.md`).
- **Setting up and upgrading a repository** without copying component folders, palettes, fonts or feedback engines: see `docs/governance/new-repository.md`.
- **Anti-drift:** `scripts/drift.mjs` enforces it here and in adopting repositories with `--root` and a `hig-drift.json`.

## Completion review

- Every issue needs an owning implementation and validation link, or an explicit linked follow-up. See `planning/issue-coverage.md` for the per-issue state.
- Catalog entries need docs, code, platform and test coverage.
- Source and bundle deltas must be measured in the owning repository.
- A matrix row is "migrated" only when its owning PR is merged and its validation is linked. Open PRs are recorded as in progress, never as migrated.
- Physical hardware results are never inferred from simulator, emulator or browser evidence.


## Contribution, ownership and admission · HIG 0.1.0
Source: docs/governance/contributing.md

# Contribution, ownership and admission · HIG 0.1.0

Issue #36. This chapter sets out how HIG stays the one maintained design system for Bloxwap. It covers who owns what, how changes are reviewed, how components enter and leave the catalog, which platforms are supported, and how a product can justify an exception. Release, semver and deprecation rules are in the release chapter. Setting up and upgrading a repository is covered in the new-repository chapter.

## Canonical ownership

| Area | Canonical owner | Others may |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Semantic tokens (colour roles, space, radius, type, motion, density), native colour spaces, contrast pairs | `bloxwap/hig` → `@bloxwap/hig-tokens` | Map roles to host variables with `var()`. They may not redefine literal values. |
| Component contracts, DOM and React Native renderers, recipes, the semantic feedback contract | `bloxwap/hig` → `@bloxwap/hig-contracts`, `-react`, `-native`, `-feedback` | Compose components and override layout in context. They may not fork a primitive's paint or geometry. |
| Font sources, families and web loaders | `bloxwap/font` → `@bloxwap/font` | HIG generates pinned native faces from Font releases. Consumers install fonts and never commit binaries. |
| Sound recipes and the Web Audio engine | `bloxwap/sfx` | HIG owns the cue mapping and preferences, and exports approved WAV cues for native. |
| Haptic presets and the web engine | `bloxwap/haptic` | HIG owns the RN adapter and the capability matrix. |
| Chart engine | `bloxwap/chart` | HIG owns chart theming and the accessible non-canvas alternative. |
| Product business logic, routing and data | The owning product repository | HIG components never import wallet, network or trading code. |
| Brand marks | `bloxwap/hig` brand component (pinned from the Font SVG) | Use the component. Exact mark fills need a dated exception. |

The organization adoption matrix (`planning/adoption.json`) records the owner, applicability, HIG version, merged PRs, status and dated exceptions for each repository and product surface.

## Contribution and review criteria

Every HIG pull request must:

1. **Link its issue** (`Part of #N` or `Closes #N`) and state its intent, the states it affects and its platform mapping.
2. **Change source and generated artifacts together**, then run `npm ci && npm run check` (build, lint, generation drift, typecheck, web and native tests). Also run the smokes relevant to the change: `smoke:ssr`, `smoke:packed`, `smoke:packed-native`, `smoke:packed-boundaries`, `smoke:packed-examples`, `examples:check` and `quality`.
3. **Cover behaviour on both renderers**, or record the platform decision and its supported alternative. Include accessible names, roles and states, keyboard and focus, native back, large text and RTL, and muted operation (sound and haptics off) without losing essential feedback.
4. **Label evidence precisely**: automated, browser, iOS Simulator, Android emulator or physical device. A mock, simulator or emulator never proves physical sound, haptics, VoiceOver or display output.
5. **List the checks that were not run**, upstream gaps, rollout and rollback. Breaking changes follow the release chapter.
6. **Pass the scoped anti-drift check** (`node scripts/drift.mjs`, run by `npm run quality` and tests). New exceptions follow the exception policy below.

A maintainer reviews against the same list. A PR that only updates screenshots or baselines must say why the visual change is intended.

## Component admission

A component or recipe enters the catalog only when all of the following hold:

- It is used repeatedly in at least two Bloxwap surfaces, or one product surface plus an SDK docs site, and the inventory (`planning/catalog.json`) cites that usage.
- It has a minimal API that composes existing primitives, with no wallet, network or trading dependencies and no unrelated imports. The per-entry export and boundary smokes enforce this.
- It has a React DOM renderer and either a React Native renderer or a documented native alternative, and the platform matrix is updated.
- It has a complete state matrix: focus, pressed, busy/disabled, error, empty, long text, large text, reduced motion, and feedback disabled where relevant. It also has catalog examples that typecheck in the packed consumers.
- It is documented: a usage chapter, an API reference, accessibility notes and a migration note for each fork it replaces.

## Component removal

1. Inventory every consumer with org-wide code search and the adoption matrix.
2. Deprecate the component in a minor release. Name the replacement, provide a codemod or checklist, and keep the export working for at least one minor release and 30 days.
3. Open removal PRs in each consuming repository, or record dated exceptions for them.
4. Remove the component in the next major release and record the change in the changelog and the matrix.

## Platform support policy

| Platform | Supported (tested in CI or recorded evidence) | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| React DOM | React 19.2; Vite, SSR and Next 16.4 (webpack) packed consumers; Chromium, Firefox and WebKit | Other bundler or Next versions need checks in the host |
| React Native | React 19.1, RN 0.81.5, Expo 54, Metro; iOS Simulator (iOS 26.5) and Android emulator (API 35) gallery runs | RN 0.83 is not certified yet (#68). Physical devices are pending (#55) |
| Tokens only | Plain CSS, Tailwind through host config, typed tokens | No React, RN or audio peers |
| Feedback | Web: `@bloxwap/sfx` and `@bloxwap/haptic`. Native: Expo audio and haptics adapters | Essential outcomes must never depend on sound or haptics |

Support only changes in a minor or major release. Each change updates `docs/architecture/platform-matrix.md`, the packed smokes and this table together.

## Justified product exceptions

A product may differ from HIG only through a recorded exception. Silent forks are not allowed.

- **Scope:** an exact path or folder prefix, and a single anti-drift rule (`obsolete-import`, `copied-palette`, `copied-token-definition`, `copied-primitive-css` or `copied-font-binary`).
- **Required fields:** `owner` (an accountable role or person), `reason` (the user or product need, or the rollback dependency) and `expires` (`YYYY-MM-DD`, at most 180 days ahead).
- **Where:** HIG's own exceptions go in `planning/drift-exceptions.json`. An adopting repository keeps its exceptions in its own `hig-drift.json`. The adoption matrix links to them.
- **Review:** the check fails on expired exceptions and on exceptions without an owner or reason, and warns about unused ones. Renewing an exception needs a new reason and owner approval. Repeated exceptions for the same need are a signal to propose a HIG change through the admission criteria.

Intentional density differences, such as compact Pro versus the comfortable touch app, are HIG density modes. They are not exceptions.

## Scoped anti-drift checks

`scripts/drift.mjs` has no dependencies and checks only files tracked in git under the configured `paths`. Paths listed under `canonical` are exempt from the copy rules.

| Rule | Fails when |
| --- | --- |
| `obsolete-import` | Code imports a retired fork (`@workspace/tokens`, `@workspace/ui`, `@workspace/ui-native`, plus repository-specific `obsoleteImports`) or a copied `vendor/hig/` or `styles/hig/` folder |
| `copied-palette` | Code hard-codes the Bloxwap brand hexes owned by `@bloxwap/hig-tokens` |
| `copied-token-definition` | A stylesheet assigns a literal value to a `--hig-*` token. Remapping one role to another with `var()` is allowed |
| `copied-primitive-css` | A bare `.hig-*` selector sets the primitive's paint or geometry (background, border, radius or min-height). Contextual layout overrides are allowed |
| `copied-font-binary` | A `.ttf`, `.otf` or `.woff*` file is committed outside a canonical font owner |

Generation drift (stale tokens, brand or glossary outputs) is checked separately by `scripts/check-drift.mjs` in `npm run lint`.


## New repository setup and upgrades · HIG 0.1.0
Source: docs/governance/new-repository.md

# New repository setup and upgrades · HIG 0.1.0

Issue #36. These steps adopt HIG in a new or existing Bloxwap repository without copying component folders, palettes, fonts or feedback engines. The five SDK docs sites followed this path: bloxwap/hyperliquid#180, bloxwap/chart#53, bloxwap/font#11, bloxwap/sfx#50 and bloxwap/haptic#26.

## 1. Pick applicability

Add or update the repository's row in `planning/adoption.json` (a PR to bloxwap/hig) with one of these applicability values:

| Applicability | Install | Never add |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Product runtime UI (web) | `@bloxwap/hig-tokens`, `-contracts`, `-react`; `@bloxwap/font` | Copied component folders or token CSS |
| Product runtime UI (React Native) | `@bloxwap/hig-tokens`, `-contracts`, `-native`, `-native-fonts`; optional `-feedback` plus Expo peers | DOM renderer imports, font binaries outside the manifest |
| Docs or marketing site | `@bloxwap/hig-tokens`, `-react` (CSS and the controls in use); `@bloxwap/font` | A local `.btn` layer, a palette copy, `vendor/hig` |
| Brand or content only | Nothing at runtime; follow the principles, content and brand chapters | React, RN or audio dependencies |
| No UI | Nothing; README and content conventions only | Any HIG runtime dependency |

## 2. Install versioned packages

HIG is not on npm yet (#56). Until it is, consume the packed candidate:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/bloxwap/hig && cd hig && git checkout <commit>
npm ci && npm run generate:fonts && npm run build
npm run release:dry-run -- --channel candidate   # local tarballs only; no publish, tag or release
```

`generate:fonts` needs Python with `fonttools[woff]==4.61.1` and `brotli==1.2.0`. In the consuming repository:

- Copy only the needed `artifacts/release-candidate/bloxwap-hig-*.tgz` files into `vendor/bloxwap-hig/`.
- Record their SHA-256 hashes and the source commit in a README or `provenance.json`.
- Depend on them with `file:` dependencies, adding `overrides` so HIG's internal dependencies resolve to the same files.

Never copy `packages/*/src`, `dist` folders, `tokens.css`, palettes, fonts or feedback engines. When #56 publishes, swap the `file:` dependencies for registry versions and delete `vendor/bloxwap-hig/`.

Then follow the installation chapter for your platform: import `@bloxwap/hig-tokens/css` and `@bloxwap/hig-react/css` once, use per-component imports, load fonts through `@bloxwap/font`, and on native register fonts from the HIG font manifest.

## 3. Add the scoped drift check to CI

Create `hig-drift.json` in the repository root:

```json
{
  "paths": ["apps/docs/app", "apps/docs/components", "apps/docs/lib", "apps/docs/styles"],
  "canonical": [],
  "obsoleteImports": [],
  "exceptions": []
}
```

Run the check from a pinned HIG checkout. The script uses only Node built-ins and needs no install:

```yaml
- uses: actions/checkout@v4
  with: {repository: bloxwap/hig, ref: <same commit as the vendored tarballs>, path: .hig}
- run: node .hig/scripts/drift.mjs --root . --config hig-drift.json
```

- **Scope:** only paths you have migrated. Widen `paths` as more surfaces move.
- **`canonical`:** use it only for assets the repository owns. For example, `bloxwap/font` owns its web font files.
- **Exceptions:** record any other exception with an owner, a reason and an expiry no more than 180 days ahead, following the contribution chapter's exception policy.

First run against current `main` heads on 2026-10-15, scanning `apps/docs` (automated, local):

- hyperliquid and haptic pass.
- sfx flags the brand-mark fill in `lib/og-card.tsx`. That needs an exception like HIG's own brand marks.
- chart flags `styles/hig-roles.generated.css`, tracked upstream in #66; [chart#54](https://github.com/bloxwap/chart/pull/54) deletes it.
- font flags its own font binaries, which belong under `canonical`.
- agent-cli flags `vendor/hig/tokens.css`, its import, and committed TTFs (#58).

## 4. Validate and record

- Build the site or app and run the repository's lint, typecheck, test and browser checks, plus keyboard, 390px mobile, large text and RTL checks.
- Measure CSS, JS and font bytes and the dependency count before and after.
- Link the merged PR, the HIG version and any dated exceptions in the matrix row.
- Label evidence as automated, browser, iOS Simulator, Android emulator or physical device.

## Upgrading HIG

1. Read the changelog in the dry-run artifact, or the npm release once #56 is done, together with the semver section of the release chapter.
2. Upgrade tokens, contracts, renderer and feedback together. Never mix candidate commits. Recompute the vendored hashes.
3. Update the drift checkout `ref` to the same commit and run the check. Remove exceptions whose need has gone.
4. Re-run the validation in step 4 and update the matrix row's `higVersion` and PR links.
5. Roll back by reverting the upgrade PR, which restores the previous tarballs and lockfile. Product pilots also keep their host feature flag (for example `NEXT_PUBLIC_HIG_PILOT=0`).


## Quality, budgets and evidence · HIG 0.1.0
Source: docs/governance/quality.md

# Quality, budgets and evidence · HIG 0.1.0

Issues #31–#32. `npm run check` executes DOM and native suites with test counts. Native module mocks demonstrate roles/state/callback/lifecycle contracts; real packed Expo/Metro consumers demonstrate platform resolution. Neither is physical output or assistive-technology certification.

Gates inspect actual generated package exports, platform imports, tokens/cue hashes, scoped anti-drift exceptions, packed consumer installs, every copyable example, SSR/hydration/StrictMode, docs static route/base paths, visual/browser states and measured gzip/assets. Negative tests deliberately introduce invalid exports, stale token output, budget regression, cross-platform imports and copied/obsolete tokens to prove failure paths.

Budgets are regression limits from the initial candidate measurements, not claims of production savings:

| Metric | Measured initial | Limit | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Individual DOM Button gzip (React external) | 706 B | 850 B | ~20% API/behavior fix headroom, overlay/audio/chart excluded |
| Individual AmountInput gzip | 325 B | 400 B | Small labelled primitive, ~23% headroom |
| Native Switch gzip (React/RN external) | 1,383 B; 1,870 B after #67 | 2,200 B | Raised for #67: the shared Text now carries the font-scale cap and Korean/Chinese script tracking, Switch the token-role track and the Android thumb token. ~18% headroom; verifies no Slider/SVG/overlay/feedback imports |
| Platform-neutral feedback contract gzip | 962 B | 1,200 B | ~25% headroom without device engines |
| Docs JS gzip, all lazy chunks | 204,877 B | 240,000 B | ~17% headroom; includes chart/code examples, not initial-load-only |
| Docs CSS | 110,618 B (with token roles, #66) | 115,000 B | ~4% headroom; raised from 110,000 B when `@bloxwap/hig-tokens/css` gained radius/type/motion/density/font roles |
| Sans + Mono assets | 592,796 B | 600,000 B | Pins two approved faces; new script/face requires explicit review |
| Native fixture faces from `@bloxwap/hig-native-fonts` (Sans 400/600, Mono 400) | 1,278,880 B | 1,400,000 B | Only the three registered faces; optional CJK and other weights stay unloaded. Every generated face hash is checked |
| Font binaries in web/shared tarballs (tokens, contracts, react, feedback, native) | 0 files | 0 files | Native faces ship only in `@bloxwap/hig-native-fonts` (#64); `release:dry-run` fails otherwise and records `packedSizes` |
| Native four-cue WAV assets | 103,618 B | 110,000 B | ~6% headroom; no full engine/catalog assets |

The actual build report is `evidence/quality-report.json`. Bundles use explicit external React/RN peers, so figures measure HIG runtime contribution, not total installed/Metro app size. Production app/Pro/native before/after deltas require owning-repository builds and reviewed baselines; do not invent a percentage improvement. Export/dependency graph reports and packed tests enforce separation, while owning migrations must measure complete apps with equal data/toolchain.

Exceptions require path/rule, owner, reason and expiry. Approved brand geometry is exempt from literal-palette detection until review; unrelated primitive/palette copies fail. New repositories should run scoped gates on migrated surfaces and keep dated residuals rather than blanket exemptions.

Physical release review remains pending: iPhone Safari, Android Chrome, native iOS and Android, VoiceOver/TalkBack, large text/RTL, color/font fidelity, actual SFX/haptic output/latency/settings/interruption/background behavior. Coordinate upstream haptic#9. Release artifacts cannot change those “pending” rows into passes.

## Versioned visual regressions

The catalog browser gate captures and runs axe on every shipped state. Button, Field and Input additionally compare eight versioned mobile/reduced-motion screenshots in `tests/visual-baselines/`, and Slider compares two keyboard-focused captures (comfortable and compact density). Geometry changes fail; pixel changes above 2% fail after a 24-channel-value antialias tolerance. `tests/visual.test.ts` deliberately changes geometry and pixels to prove the gate fails. Baselines record current candidate rendering, not approved product parity or native-device fidelity. Review an intentional change using CI captures, then run `HIG_UPDATE_VISUALS=1 node scripts/catalog-browser-smoke.mjs` against the production docs preview and commit the reviewed baseline images.


## Release candidates, semver and rollback · HIG 0.1.0
Source: docs/governance/release.md

# Release candidates, semver and rollback · HIG 0.1.0

Issue #32. This task's automation is **dry-run only**. It never invokes npm publication, GitHub release or git tag creation. Unsupported flags fail before artifact creation. No npm credentials are requested or used.

```sh
npm ci
npm run check
npm run examples:check
npm run quality
npm run smoke:packed
npm run smoke:packed-native
npm run smoke:packed-next
npm run smoke:packed-css
npm run release:dry-run -- --channel candidate
npm run release:dry-run -- --channel stable-simulation
```

Candidate mode stages `0.1.0-candidate.sha<commit>` package metadata and matching internal dependency versions. Stable-simulation stages the coordinated source version. Runtime contract/docs source version and source commit are recorded explicitly; neither source files nor git refs are version-mutated by the dry run. Both produce local tarballs, checked export/types/CSS/assets/files/dependency manifests, hashes, changelog, copied docs artifact and provenance report. `npm pack --ignore-scripts` packs already validated outputs, never publishes. Physical claims remain pending in every report.

CI checks out PR source, installs locked peers, executes web/native/SSR/Metro/example/visual/accessibility/budget gates and uploads review artifacts. A provenance record identifies source commit, package/contract/docs versions and hashes; it is not an npm registry provenance attestation or a release. Artifact inspection checks exports, licenses, optional peers and only approved assets. No example app implementation is included in runtime packages.

Publication gates are tracked in `planning/release-blockers.json`:

- npm credentials are not configured on the release machine (#56).
- Physical devices and assistive technology (#55).
- Upstream feedback gaps (#70).
- Owning product migrations that are still open (#33, #35).

A dry run cannot turn these into passes, and renaming a candidate does not publish v1.

Semver:

- **Major:** breaking changes to token meaning or appearance, typography scale, layout, accessibility or action behaviour, or semantic feedback mapping.
- **Minor:** compatible additions.
- **Patch:** verified fixes.

Deprecation names the alternative, a migration codemod or checklist, and the owning consumers from `planning/adoption.json`. A deprecated export keeps working for at least one minor release and 30 days, and is removed only in the next major release after consumer PRs are merged or have dated exceptions (see the contribution chapter). Keep code/examples/API/citations at the same source commit; separate package prerelease identifiers are explicit in artifact metadata.

Rollback for an owning pilot: keep the previous package artifacts and lockfile, disable the host feature flag, restore prior renderer/backend imports and rebuild. Keep saved feedback/business data backward-compatible; never erase prior choices. Remove old assets only after production and physical-device proof. A future published rollback would require separate release authorization and package provenance; this task performs none.


## Installation and citation · HIG 0.1.0
Source: docs/installation.md

# Installation and citation · HIG 0.1.0

These are review candidates, not published npm packages. Use local dry-run tarballs or CI artifact downloads; do not assume `@bloxwap/hig-*` is available on the registry. Published-style imports in examples are tested against packed candidates. Version references identify a candidate until release gates are complete.

## React / Vite

Run `npm ci && npm run build && npm run smoke:packed`. The smoke script installs tarballs into an independent temporary consumer and builds the fixture. For a host app install tokens, contracts and React tarballs plus React/DOM 19.2. Import `@bloxwap/hig-tokens/css` and `@bloxwap/hig-react/css` once; import individual components such as `@bloxwap/hig-react/button`. Pin @bloxwap/font 0.1.2 and choose only the required families/scripts using asset URL @font-face rules named `'Bloxwap Sans'` and `'Bloxwap Mono'`; HIG controls read `--hig-font-sans`/`--hig-font-mono`, which fall back to those literal families. The included fixture has Sans and Mono only, and its browser smoke checks that `.hig-button` and `.hig-number` render loaded Bloxwap faces. Never copy font binaries or component folders.

### Radix overlay peers and Fumadocs

The four Radix packages are optional peers with caret ranges: `@radix-ui/react-dialog ^1.1.15`, `@radix-ui/react-popover ^1.1.15`, `@radix-ui/react-dropdown-menu ^2.1.16` and `@radix-ui/react-tooltip ^1.2.8`. Install them only for `@bloxwap/hig-react/overlay`, `@bloxwap/hig-react/recipes` or `@bloxwap/hig-react/recipes/trade-entry` (dialog only). Hosts that already use Radix, such as Fumadocs, share their copy: `npm run smoke:packed-fumadocs` installs the packed React tarball next to fumadocs-ui 16.17.3 with strict peers and `npm ci`, asserts every `@radix-ui/*` package appears once, and renders the overlays on the resolved current releases. The workspace fixtures keep testing the lower bounds. Do not set `legacy-peer-deps` for HIG.

## SSR and Next client boundaries

Run `npm run smoke:ssr`, `npm run build:next` and `npm run smoke:packed-next`. Token/formatting imports and button/provider SSR are deterministic. Components with hooks carry `use client` in their emitted modules. In Next, import HIG CSS in the app layout and put interactive example state in a client component; keep wallet/network logic with the host. Next's published Bloxwap font loaders remain owned upstream.

Fonts in Next: put the `@bloxwap/font` loader variables on `<html>`, for example `<html className={`${BloxwapSans.variable} ${BloxwapMono.variable}`}>`. The loaders register hashed family names, so HIG never matches a literal `'Bloxwap Sans'` there. Instead `--hig-font-sans` and `--hig-font-mono` in `@bloxwap/hig-tokens/css` resolve `var(--font-bloxwap-sans)` and `var(--font-bloxwap-mono)` first and fall back to the literal families. No bridge CSS is needed. If a host keeps its own variable names, override the roles on `:root` after importing the tokens CSS: `:root { --hig-font-sans: var(--my-sans), 'Bloxwap Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; }`. The variables must be defined on `<html>` (not `<body>`), because the roles resolve on `:root`. `npm run smoke:packed-next` serves the packed consumer and checks, in Chromium, that `.hig-button` and `.hig-number` compute to a loaded Bloxwap face (`document.fonts.check` plus the `FontFace` status). Next 16.4.0 (webpack), React 19.2 and the published Bloxwap Sans Next loader are verified in the dedicated production fixture; other Next versions require host checks. Verify hydration, stable IDs and StrictMode before adopting a host version.

## Expo / React Native

Run `npm run smoke:packed-native` after packed artifacts are built, or `npm run start -w hig-native-fixture` for the device gallery. Matrix: React 19.1, RN 0.81.5, Expo 54, Metro as locked. Native consumers install tokens/contracts/native tarballs; optional feedback installs its tarball and explicit Expo backend peers. Slider and SVG peers are only needed by their family entries. Import `@bloxwap/hig-native/button`, not the DOM renderer. Dynamic Type remains enabled; native targets stay 48. Keyboard/safe-area/back behavior belongs to the native host and its supported OS.

Install Expo native peers with `npx expo install` (for example `expo-asset ~12.0.13` and `expo-constants ~18.0.14` alongside `expo-font`/`expo-audio`). Expo 54 autolinking links the copy resolved from the app root; a hoisted SDK 57 `expo-asset` pulled by `expo-audio`'s `*` peer compiles away and the app fails at launch with `Cannot find native module 'ExpoAsset'` (observed on the iOS Simulator). `verifyExpoNativeModules` in `scripts/native-compatibility.mjs` guards the fixture and packed consumer. `HIGProvider` follows the OS layout direction (`I18nManager.isRTL`) unless `direction` is passed.

`@bloxwap/hig-native` ships one small Android library (`android/`, `com.bloxwap.hig.HIGPackage`) that React Native and Expo autolinking pick up in development and release builds (`npx expo prebuild`, `npx expo run:android`). It adds Android set-progress to `Slider`; nothing else depends on it, and in Expo Go the Slider falls back to increment/decrement only. iOS needs no native code.

Simulator/emulator verification: `scripts/native-sim/` builds the packed candidate gallery as real Release apps and drives them with XCUITest (iOS Simulator) and UiAutomation instrumentation, uiautomator and TalkBack (Android emulator). Results and residual physical-hardware limits are in `evidence/native-sim/`.

WOFF2 is not a native font asset. `@bloxwap/hig-native-fonts` ships 15 static Bloxwap Sans/Mono (plus Korean and Simplified Chinese Sans) TTFs generated reproducibly from pinned Font 0.1.2 sources, with a typed `fontManifest` export and `@bloxwap/hig-native-fonts/manifest`. Install it alongside the tokens, contracts and native tarballs, then `require('@bloxwap/hig-native-fonts/fonts/BloxwapSans.ttf')` and register the faces with expo-font before setting the native provider fontFamily, as the gallery does. `@bloxwap/hig-tokens` no longer contains font binaries (#64); see [native font migration](migration/native.md#native-fonts-moved-out-of-hig-tokens). Rasterization on physical displays remains part of #55. New repositories follow `docs/governance/new-repository.md`.

## Tokens only / plain CSS / Tailwind

Install the tokens tarball alone and import CSS variables or typed tokens. No React/RN/audio peer is required. Plain HTML uses semantic `--hig-*` roles.

`@bloxwap/hig-tokens/css` defines every role a plain CSS host needs, so nobody has to read the manifest or generate role files:

| Roles | Example | Values |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Color | `--hig-surface`, `--hig-action` | sRGB, then OKLCH/P3 in `@supports` |
| Space | `--hig-space-md` | `xs`–`xxxl`, `section`, in rem |
| Font | `--hig-font-sans`, `--hig-font-mono` | `@bloxwap/font` Next variable, then literal family |
| Radius | `--hig-radius-md`, `--hig-radius-pill` | `sm` `md` `lg` `xl` in rem; `pill` 9999px |
| Type | `--hig-type-body-size`, `--hig-type-body-line-height`, `--hig-type-body-weight`, `--hig-type-body` | `caption` `label` `body` `title` `display`; the bare role is a `font` shorthand in Sans |
| Motion | `--hig-motion-duration-base`, `--hig-motion-easing-standard` | `fast` `base` `slow` ms; 0ms under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` or `[data-hig-motion='reduced']` |
| Density | `--hig-density-control`, `--hig-density-compact-gap` | `control` `target` `gap` per mode; the unprefixed roles follow `[data-hig-density='compact']` |

```css
@import '@bloxwap/hig-tokens/css';
.card { border-radius: var(--hig-radius-lg); padding: var(--hig-space-lg); font: var(--hig-type-body); }
.card h2 { font: var(--hig-type-title); }
.card button { min-height: var(--hig-density-control); transition: background var(--hig-motion-duration-fast) var(--hig-motion-easing-standard); }
```

`npm run smoke:packed-css` proves this path. It installs only the packed `@bloxwap/hig-tokens` tarball into an empty consumer, links `@bloxwap/hig-tokens/css` from a script-free HTML page whose own stylesheet uses nothing but the roles, and checks the computed radius, type, motion and density values in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, including 0ms durations under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` and `[data-hig-motion='reduced']` and the compact values under `[data-hig-density='compact']`. It fails if the page requests anything other than the HTML, its stylesheet and the token CSS, so the manifest is never read.

Tailwind may reference these values through host configuration; HIG does not require content scans or a shadcn registry. Native uses dp and explicit hex/channel maps; do not feed CSS functions or rename rem to dp. The audited monorepo web/native rem roots are both 16; HIG supports StyleSheet rather than claiming a verified NativeWind consumer. See the source-reconciliation chapter for native font generation and registration.

## Optional chart, sound and haptics

Chart is DOM-only and lazy; install @bloxwap/chart 0.3.0 for that entry and supply a textual summary. Native uses labeled readouts/lists. Feedback install paths, preferences, iOS physical-tap limitations and Expo backends are in the feedback chapters. Keep essential outcome text available with both channels off.

## Stable citations and upgrades

Cite “Bloxwap HIG 0.1.0 candidate, chapter/anchor” plus an immutable GitHub commit permalink. Branch and docs preview links are mutable. Upgrade tokens, contracts, renderer, docs/examples and semantic cue mapping together; compare API behavior and adopt behind a rollback flag. Token appearance and accessibility behavior changes require semver review. No publication, release or tag is performed by this implementation.

The native fixture pins React **19.1.0**, matching the RN 0.81.5 renderer exactly. Web/Next/Fumadocs fixtures use React 19.2.0. Metro explicitly resolves every native `react`/`react/*` import to the native fixture's version so shared-workspace code cannot load web React. Quality and packed-native checks compare the installed version to RN's actual renderer guard; a successful Metro bundle alone does not prove runtime compatibility.


## Native application pilot (#35)
Source: docs/migration/native.md

# Native application pilot (#35)

Owner: bloxwap/monorepo maintainers (named assignment in #57). Status on 2026-10-15: [monorepo#4540](https://github.com/bloxwap/monorepo/pull/4540) migrates the app's settings, entry, logout, sound card and demo number to HIG `0.1.0-candidate.sha7c67a07c`, with one HIG feedback controller and 15 duplicate fonts removed. It was verified on the iOS Simulator and Android emulator, but it is not merged yet (it needs the required human `signoff`). Physical-device certification is tracked in #55 and React Native 0.83 certification in #68. No tactile, audible or VoiceOver observation is claimed.

Pilot: font registration → dp/sRGB token mapping → amount/selection/review sheet → visible async outcome → independent feedback settings. The Expo gallery proves candidate packaging and contract examples, not the owning app's native build.

Checklist:
- [ ] Record actual RN/Expo/Metro/autolinking versions, source commit, old ui-native/token/font/audio wrappers, screenshots and native bundle/assets/latency baseline.
- [ ] Register the pinned static TTF faces from `@bloxwap/hig-native-fonts` and its typed `fontManifest`; register before setting family. Do not treat WOFF2 or an invented native family as success.
- [ ] Map dp and legacy NativeWind rem roots explicitly. Keep Dynamic Type, 48 targets, logical RTL layout, safe areas, keyboard avoidance, native back and labelled fields/errors.
- [ ] Preview native import codemods, using individual switch/checkbox/range entries; wire optional SVG/Slider/Expo audio/haptic peers only where used. Retain platform-specific descriptions and host callbacks.
- [ ] Preserve raw financial strings, order/network logic, stable list identity and quiet live numbers. Use labelled list/readout native chart alternative unless a real supported native engine is reviewed.
- [ ] Read old sound/haptic settings with a host migration adapter before writing v1 key. Keep explicit false choices, volume and motion independent; handle corrupt/missing storage conservatively.
- [ ] Hook AppState/interruption/background and dispose cached players/listeners. Test muted channels, missing assets, backend rejection, repeated values, busy/disabled, canceled scroll/drag and unsupported hardware.
- [ ] Build the real app for iOS and Android. Observe large text, long translations, Arabic/Hebrew RTL, VoiceOver/TalkBack, orientation, keyboard/sheets, reduced motion and every feedback combination on devices.
- [ ] Record actual device/OS/settings and audible/tactile output, latency, silent-mode/interruption/background behavior. Reuse upstream haptic#9 review; simulator/mocks remain API evidence only.
- [ ] Remove duplicated source/assets/backend wrappers after device builds confirm references and autolinking are gone; quantify before/after sizes with equal toolchain/data.
- [ ] Link owning rollout PR and remaining version/exception work into the matrix.

## Native fonts moved out of hig-tokens

Issue #64. Up to `0.1.0-candidate.sha7c67a07c`, `@bloxwap/hig-tokens` shipped the 15 static TTFs under `@bloxwap/hig-tokens/fonts/*`. Web-only consumers never served them, but they made up most of the tarball. They now live in `@bloxwap/hig-native-fonts`. The bytes, file names, registration keys and SHA-256 hashes are unchanged.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| `require('@bloxwap/hig-tokens/fonts/BloxwapSans.ttf')` | `require('@bloxwap/hig-native-fonts/fonts/BloxwapSans.ttf')` |
| `@bloxwap/hig-tokens/fonts/manifest.json` | `@bloxwap/hig-native-fonts/manifest`, or the typed `fontManifest` export |
| `@bloxwap/hig-tokens/fonts/OFL.txt` | `@bloxwap/hig-native-fonts/fonts/OFL.txt` |

- **Expo / React Native:** add the `bloxwap-hig-native-fonts-*.tgz` tarball next to tokens, contracts and native (with a matching `overrides` entry when vendoring), then replace the import prefix. `nativeFont(fontManifest, 'BloxwapSans', 600)` from `@bloxwap/hig-contracts` returns the registration key. Hashes you already pinned stay valid.
- **Satori / OG images in web repositories:** these also read static TTFs (bloxwap/chart's OG card is one). Install `@bloxwap/hig-native-fonts` as a build-time dependency for that script only, or read the TTF from `@bloxwap/font` if it ships one. Never copy the faces into the repository.
- **Web-only hosts:** remove nothing. They keep loading fonts from `@bloxwap/font`, and their tokens tarball shrinks. `npm run release:dry-run` fails if any web or shared tarball contains `.ttf`, `.otf` or `.woff*` files, and it records the packed sizes in `packedSizes` in the release report.
- **Coordination:** monorepo#4540 loads the faces from `@bloxwap/hig-tokens`. Rebase it on a candidate that includes this change, and switch it to the new prefix when it does.

Rollback: host feature flag restores old renderer/backends and previous lockfile. Persisted business data and feedback choices retain old-compatible fields during staged rollout; avoid one-way preference deletion. Keep old static assets until both physical platforms pass.

## Five SDK documentation pilots (#34)

# Five SDK documentation pilots (#34)

Owner: each SDK repository's docs maintainers (named assignment in #57). Preserve each interactive SDK demo and its host APIs; HIG replaces shared presentation only. Status on 2026-10-15: all five sites consume the vendored HIG `0.1.0-candidate.sha7c67a07c` packages. Each was merged after independent verification: [hyperliquid#180](https://github.com/bloxwap/hyperliquid/pull/180), [chart#53](https://github.com/bloxwap/chart/pull/53), [font#11](https://github.com/bloxwap/font/pull/11), [sfx#50](https://github.com/bloxwap/sfx/pull/50) and [haptic#26](https://github.com/bloxwap/haptic/pull/26). | Repository | Shared presentation | Distinctive feature to preserve | Remaining owner validation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

## Compact source comparison

The October 14 review of the five local checkout revisions found the following
presentation baseline. These are source line counts, including product-specific
styles, comments and formatting; they are not an estimate of removable CSS.

| Site revision | Global CSS lines | Migration difference |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| [Hyperliquid 53159f1](https://github.com/bloxwap/hyperliquid/tree/53159f1/apps/docs) | 1,034 | Semantic color aliases and 160 ms interaction timing. |
| [Chart 8c71c71](https://github.com/bloxwap/chart/tree/8c71c71/apps/docs) | 440 | Nunito/Maple Mono remain; preserve chart previews. |

Hyperliquid, Chart and SFX have byte-identical 172-line token snapshots;
Haptic's declarations match with a different provenance comment. Chart, SFX
and Haptic also repeat the same button and search recipes. Use the existing
HIG token/component packages for shared behavior, and keep the written guide
compact with **rule → token or recipe → exception** rather than duplicating the
five implementations.


## Documentation website and migration shell · HIG 0.1.0
Source: docs/website.md

# Documentation website and migration shell · HIG 0.1.0

HIG uses Next.js static export and Fumadocs, matching the sibling SDK sites. SFX and Haptic pin `fumadocs-core`/`fumadocs-ui` 16.17.1, `fumadocs-mdx` 15.4.7 and Next 16.4.0; HIG uses those versions. Font uses 16.15.17/15.4.5/16.3.6 and Chart 16.15.14/15.4.5/16.3.6. React 19.2 satisfies the current Fumadocs peer contract.

`docs/` Markdown chapters are the single normative source. The trading glossary is the exception: `docs/foundations/glossary.json` is authored and `docs/foundations/glossary.md` is generated. `scripts/generate-docs.mjs` generates the ignored `apps/docs/content/docs` collection, `meta.json` navigation, Markdown downloads, catalog data and `llms.txt`. Do not edit generated guides. Component reference pages derive from published package declarations and `planning/examples.json`; they link to the normative family guide. `npm run generate:examples` emits runnable web/native previews; `npm run examples:check` compiles all code variants.

`apps/docs/source.config.ts` defines the MDX collection; `lib/source.ts` supplies the page tree. `app/docs/[[...slug]]` renders Fumadocs titles, TOCs, code, navigation and source/edit links. `components/provider.tsx` and `search.tsx` provide the dark theme and static Orama search at `search.json`. Fonts, palette and preview controls import the shipped Bloxwap font and HIG packages. Fumadocs owns the responsive navigation, accessible search dialog and document shell.

Run `npm ci`, then `bun docs:dev` or `npm run docs:dev`. Turbo's terminal UI prepares package declarations, examples and guides before starting Next at `http://localhost:3905/`, with documents under `/docs/`. `npm run dev:docs` is an alias. Use `bun docs:dev --ui=stream` for plain terminal logs. `bun docs:check` and `bun docs:build` also prepare their required package outputs.

`npm run build:docs` generates the collection, builds Next and copies its static export to `apps/docs/dist`. Preview with `bun docs:preview` at `http://localhost:4174/hig/`. The static build defaults to `/hig`, while development defaults to the host root; override `NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_PATH` without a trailing slash and `HIG_DOCS_ORIGIN` for another host. Every canonical document lives under `/docs/`. Explicit static redirect documents retain the previous `/guides/*`, `/components/*` and `/catalog/` URLs, including their query and fragment. Sitemap, Markdown and LLM exports ship in the same artifact. No deployment is part of the build.

The homepage retains the bounded playground: App/Pro/Docs presets, supported states, locale/direction contracts, independent sound/haptics/motion settings, volume, matching Get Code, and validated share configuration. Native examples are real RN components in the Expo gallery. Device screenshots, VoiceOver/TalkBack and physical feedback observations remain pending. Live examples use sample host-owned actions and never submit orders or call a wallet.

## Reusing the shell for issue #34

Each SDK keeps its own content and distinctive demo: Hyperliquid market playground, Chart preview, Font type tester, SFX sound board, Haptic interaction demos. Start with HIG's `next.config.mjs`, PostCSS/source config, `lib/source.ts`, root/docs layouts, provider/search and MDX component mapping. Set the product title, repository, base path and port. Copy the shell code as a starting template, then import the versioned HIG token CSS, React CSS and font assets rather than copying palette values or primitive implementations. Keep the SDK's existing `content/docs` as its normative collection, or generate it from one existing Markdown source as HIG does; never maintain two authored guides.

Place SDK demos behind a client boundary like `components/demo.tsx`; keep documentation server-rendered and searchable. Compose HIG install/copy/code/callout controls in those demos. Preserve each SDK's static search, llms.txt, sitemap, metadata and legacy URLs. Match the production base path during browser tests. Run build, lint, typecheck, example checks and the docs gates, capture desktop/mobile pages and the distinctive demo, and record exceptions and package versions in the #34 migration matrix. This HIG change provides the shell; it does not claim the five separate SDK migrations are complete.

## Validation

`npm run check` includes the Next build and docs typecheck. CI runs production browser gates against the exported site, including the playground, search/navigation, legacy deep links, code tabs, all component states, runtime errors and axe checks. Screenshots and browser reports are uploaded with the static export as review artifacts. Publication, tagging and deployment remain separate operations.

The separate Documentation workflow builds and typechecks the static site for pull requests and pushes to `main`. After a successful build on `main`, it publishes `apps/docs/out` to [GitHub Pages](https://bloxwap.github.io/hig/) using the `/hig` base path. Pages uses GitHub Actions as its publishing source. This publishes the candidate documentation; package releases and tags remain separate operations. The workflow can also be run manually from `main` to redeploy.

The Fumadocs/Next framework changes the whole-export asset baseline: approximately 587 KB gzip of JavaScript and 95 KB CSS across all split routes (previous Vite budgets: 240 KB gzip and 22 KB). The new whole-export ceilings are 650 KB gzip and 110 KB CSS. This measures every chunk, not one page load. Font loading remains Latin Sans/Mono from upstream package files through `next/font/local`, avoiding the all-script loader’s roughly 13 MB export; the existing 600 KB font ceiling is retained.
